计算硬件 · 芯片、内存、GPU 和 CUDA、大模型、具身智能Computing hardware · Chips, memory, GPUs and CUDA, large models, embodied AI

芯片里的一秒钟One Second in Silicon

在厨房里，你对一台机器人说："把那杯水递给我。"它听见了，转头找到台面上那杯水，开过去，伸手抓起来，再开到你面前，等你的手接住才松开，前后十秒钟。这十秒里，它身上几十块芯片一刻不停：相机每秒交出几十张照片，关节每秒报告上千次自己的角度，一个几十亿参数的模型每秒看十次世界、想好接下来怎么动，每个电机里的小芯片每秒调两万次电流；也许远处的数据中心里，还有几块 GPU 在替它想一个更难的问题。这一篇从零讲起：芯片是什么，一行程序怎样变成芯片里的电流，大模型为什么要那么大、那么快的内存，为什么大多数人选 NVIDIA 的 GPU、CUDA 又是什么、别的芯片走到了哪一步，一个词怎样在硬件里走一圈，数据中心为什么要那么多显存、GPU 和光纤。然后回到机器人：它每秒吞进多少数据，各块芯片的钟怎样对齐，想要一边看、一边想、一边动，需要什么样的芯片。最后看芯片的前沿，和那些还没走出实验室、却可能解决这些问题的技术。In the kitchen, you say to a robot: "Pass me that glass of water." It hears you, turns its head and finds the glass on the worktop, drives over, reaches out and picks it up, then drives up to you and lets go only once your hand has taken it: ten seconds in all. Throughout those ten seconds, dozens of chips in its body never stop for a moment: the cameras deliver dozens of pictures a second, the joints report their angles a thousand times a second, a model with billions of parameters looks at the world ten times a second and decides how to move next, and a small chip in each motor adjusts the current 20,000 times a second; perhaps, in a distant data centre, a few GPUs are also thinking through a harder question for it. This page starts from zero: what a chip is; how a line of code becomes electric currents inside a chip; why large models need such big and such fast memory; why most people choose NVIDIA’s GPUs, what CUDA is, and how far other chips have got; how one token makes its way round the hardware; and why data centres need so much GPU memory, so many GPUs and so much optical fibre. Then we come back to the robot: how much data it takes in every second, how the clocks of its many chips are aligned, and what kind of chips it needs to look, think and move all at the same time. Finally we look at the frontier of chips, and at the technologies that have not yet left the lab but might solve these problems.

单位约定：比特（bit，记作 b）是一个 0 或 1，字节（byte，记作 B）是 8 个比特；网速常用 Gb/s（每秒十亿比特），内存带宽常用 GB/s（每秒十亿字节），差 8 倍。k、M、G、T、P 依次是千、百万、十亿、万亿、千万亿（103、106、109、1012、1015）；本篇的 GB 都是 109 字节。时间：1 ms（毫秒）是千分之一秒，1 µs（微秒）是百万分之一秒，1 ns（纳秒）是十亿分之一秒。FLOP 是一次浮点运算（一次加法或一次乘法），FLOPS 是每秒做多少次；能量用焦耳（J），功率用瓦（W，每秒多少焦耳），1 pJ（皮焦）是 10−12 J。Units: a bit (written b) is a single 0 or 1, and a byte (written B) is 8 bits; network speeds are usually given in Gb/s (billions of bits per second) and memory bandwidth in GB/s (billions of bytes per second), a factor of 8 apart. k, M, G, T and P stand in turn for thousand, million, billion, trillion and quadrillion (103, 106, 109, 1012, 1015); on this page a GB is always 109 bytes. Time: 1 ms (millisecond) is a thousandth of a second, 1 µs (microsecond) a millionth of a second and 1 ns (nanosecond) a billionth of a second. A FLOP is one floating-point operation (one addition or one multiplication), and FLOPS is how many are done per second; energy is measured in joules (J) and power in watts (W, joules per second), and 1 pJ (picojoule) is 10−12 J.

芯片和时钟Chips and clocks

f, tpath
时钟频率（Hz，GHz = 109 次/秒）；一拍里最长的那条信号路径要走多久（第 ① 步）。第 ⑭ 步里 f 是每根线每秒传几个比特（Gb/s）clock frequency (Hz; GHz = 109 times a second); how long a signal takes to travel the longest path in one clock cycle (step ①). In step ⑭, f is how many bits each wire carries per second (Gb/s)
P, α, C, V
动态功耗 P ≈ α C V² f：α 是每拍有多大比例的晶体管翻转，C 是要充放电的电容，V 是电压（第 ① 步）。第 ⑦ 步里不带下标的 P 是实际跑出的算力（FLOPS），第 ⑮ 步里 P 又是功率dynamic power P ≈ α C V² f: α is the fraction of transistors that switch in each clock cycle, C is the capacitance to be charged and discharged, V is the voltage (step ①). In step ⑦, P without a subscript is the compute actually achieved (FLOPS), and in step ⑮ P is power again
Ninst, CPI
程序的指令条数；平均每条指令要几拍（第 ② 步）the number of instructions in a program; how many clock cycles an instruction takes on average (step ②)
ppm
百万分之一：晶振的频率偏差，±20 ppm 就是每秒差 ±20 µs（第 ⑪ 步）one part in a million: the frequency error of a crystal oscillator; ±20 ppm means being off by ±20 µs every second (step ⑪)

存储和带宽Memory and bandwidth

S, N, b
模型参数占的字节数 S = N · b：N 是参数个数（"8B"就是 80 亿），b 是每个参数几字节（BF16 是 2，FP8 是 1，FP4 是 0.5）（第 ③ 步）。第 ⑤ 步里 S 是整件事快了几倍the bytes a model’s parameters take up, S = N · b: N is the number of parameters ("8B" means 8 billion), b is the bytes per parameter (2 for BF16, 1 for FP8, 0.5 for FP4) (step ③). In step ⑤, S is how many times faster the whole job gets
BW
带宽：每秒能搬多少字节（GB/s、TB/s）（第 ③ 步）bandwidth: how many bytes can be moved per second (GB/s, TB/s) (step ③)
w
内存数据线的根数（位宽）：HBM4 是 2048，机器人模块的 LPDDR5X 是 256（第 ⑭ 步）the number of data lines to the memory (its width in bits): 2048 for HBM4, 256 for the LPDDR5X on the robot’s module (step ⑭)
tread, rtok
把参数读一遍的时间；一个人用时每秒最多生成几个词元（第 ③ 步）the time to read all the parameters once; the most tokens per second it can generate for a single user (step ③)

运算和能量Operations and energy

MAC, FLOP
一次乘加；一次浮点运算（一次乘加算 2 次）（第 ④ 步）one multiply–accumulate; one floating-point operation (a multiply–accumulate counts as 2) (step ④)
FLOPS, TOPS
每秒浮点运算次数；每秒万亿次（整数）运算。T = 1012，P = 1015floating-point operations per second; trillions of (integer) operations per second. T = 1012, P = 1015
eop, ebit
做一次运算的能量；搬一个比特的能量（pJ = 10−12 J）（第 ④ 步）the energy of one operation; the energy to move one bit (pJ = 10−12 J) (step ④)
I, I*
算术强度：每搬一个字节做几次运算；屋顶线的拐点 I* = Ppeak / BW（第 ⑦ 步）arithmetic intensity: how many operations are done for each byte moved; the ridge point of the roofline, I* = Ppeak / BW (step ⑦)
Ppeak, η
芯片的峰值算力；实际能用上的比例（第 ③、⑦、⑫ 步）a chip’s peak compute; the fraction of it actually put to use (steps ③, ⑦ and ⑫)

大模型Large models

T, L
上下文里已有的词元数；层数（第 ⑦ 步）。第 ② 步里 T 是程序跑完的时间，第 ⑩ 步里 L 是损失the number of tokens already in the context; the number of layers (step ⑦). In step ②, T is the time a program takes to run, and in step ⑩, L is the loss
hkv, dh
每层几组键值头；每个头的向量长度（第 ⑦ 步）the number of key-value heads in each layer; the length of each head’s vector (step ⑦)
MKV
键值缓存占的字节数（第 ⑦ 步）the bytes the KV cache takes up (step ⑦)
G, tar
模型切成几份、放在几块 GPU 上；一次全规约的时间（第 ⑧、⑨ 步）the number of pieces the model is split into, spread over that many GPUs; the time for one all-reduce (steps ⑧ and ⑨)
C, D
训练的总运算次数 C ≈ 6ND；训练用的词元数（第 ⑩ 步）the total number of operations in training, C ≈ 6ND; the number of tokens used for training (step ⑩)
E, A, B, α, β
第 ⑩ 步里规模定律拟合出的常数；这里的 α 和功耗公式里的 α 无关；第 ④ 步里 E 是一次计算花的能量constants fitted for the scaling law in step ⑩; this α has nothing to do with the α in the power formula; in step ④, E is the energy one computation takes

机器人The robot

R, nimg
每秒涌进来的原始字节数；一张图变成几个词元（第 ⑪ 步）。第 ⑮ 步里 R 是每秒做的运算次数the raw bytes pouring in each second; how many tokens one image becomes (step ⑪). In step ⑮, R is the number of operations done per second
θ, δ
PTP 算出的两个钟的偏差；消息单程走了多久（第 ⑪ 步）the offset between two clocks, as worked out by PTP; how long a message takes to travel one way (step ⑪)
tcall, fcall
模型算一次的时间；每秒算几次（第 ⑫ 步）the time for one call of the model; how many calls it makes per second (step ⑫)
tloop
一个环从测到动起来的总时间（第 ⑬ 步）the total time a loop takes from measuring to moving (step ⑬)

缩写Abbreviations

CPU, GPU
中央处理器；图形处理器，现在主要拿来做并行计算（第 ⑤ 步）central processing unit; graphics processing unit, now used mainly for parallel computing (step ⑤)
ASIC, TPU
专用芯片；Google 为神经网络做的专用芯片（第 ⑤ 步）application-specific integrated circuit; the chip Google built specially for neural networks (step ⑤)
FPGA, MCU
现场可编程门阵列，能重新接线的芯片；单片机（第 ⑤ 步）field-programmable gate array, a chip that can be rewired; microcontroller (step ⑤)
SoC, ISP
片上系统，CPU、GPU 等做在一块芯片上；图像信号处理器（第 ⑤ 步）system on chip, with a CPU, a GPU and more on one chip; image signal processor (step ⑤)
IMU, MEMS
惯性测量单元，测角速度和加速度；微机电结构（第 ⑤ 步）inertial measurement unit, which measures angular velocity and acceleration; micro-electro-mechanical systems (step ⑤)
SRAM, DRAM
静态存储器（6 个晶体管一位）；动态存储器（1 个晶体管加 1 个电容一位）（第 ③ 步）static RAM (6 transistors per bit); dynamic RAM (1 transistor plus 1 capacitor per bit) (step ③)
HBM, LPDDR
高带宽内存，叠起来贴着 GPU；低功耗 DRAM，手机和机器人用（第 ③ 步）high-bandwidth memory, stacked up right next to the GPU; low-power DRAM, used in phones and robots (step ③)
PCIe, NVLink
CPU 和 GPU 之间的通用连线；NVIDIA 的 GPU 之间的连线（第 ②、⑨ 步）the general-purpose link between a CPU and a GPU; NVIDIA’s link between GPUs (steps ② and ⑨)
FP32, BF16, FP8, FP4
32、16、8、4 位的浮点数格式（第 ④ 步）32-, 16-, 8- and 4-bit floating-point formats (step ④)
CUDA, SM, warp
NVIDIA 的 GPU 编程平台；GPU 里的"大核"；同时执行同一条指令的 32 个线程（第 ⑥ 步）NVIDIA’s platform for programming GPUs; a "big core" inside a GPU; 32 threads that execute the same instruction at the same time (step ⑥)
KV cache
键值缓存（第 ⑦ 步）key-value cache (step ⑦)
VLA
视觉–语言–动作模型（第 ⑫ 步）vision-language-action model (step ⑫)
PTP
精确时间协议，IEEE 1588（第 ⑪ 步）Precision Time Protocol, IEEE 1588 (step ⑪)
CPO
共封装光学：把光收发器做进交换芯片的封装（第 ⑭ 步）co-packaged optics: building the optical transceivers into the switch chip’s package (step ⑭)

第 0 步 · 开场Step 0 · Opening

一杯水，十秒钟A glass of water, ten seconds

整篇只用这一个场景，先把它说清楚。还是第 5 篇和第 12 篇的那间厨房。机器人有一个带两个轮子的底盘，一根能升降的躯干，两条各有 7 个关节的手臂，手臂末端是夹爪；头能左右、上下转。它身上的传感器是这些：The whole page uses just this one scene, so let’s describe it properly first. It is the same kitchen as on pages 5 and 12. The robot has a base with two wheels, a torso that can be raised and lowered, and two arms with 7 joints each, ending in grippers; its head can turn left and right, and up and down. These are its sensors:

  • 头上一台彩色相机（1280 × 720 像素，每秒 30 帧）和一台深度相机（848 × 480，每秒 30 帧）；两只手腕上各一台小相机（640 × 480，每秒 30 帧）。On the head, a colour camera (1280 × 720 pixels, 30 frames a second) and a depth camera (848 × 480, 30 frames a second); on each wrist, a small camera (640 × 480, 30 frames a second).
  • 四个麦克风，每个每秒记 16000 个数，和第 12 篇那段录音一样。Four microphones, each recording 16000 numbers a second, as in the recording on page 12.
  • 底盘里一个 IMU（惯性测量单元，测转动和加速度），每秒 1000 次。An IMU in the base (inertial measurement unit, which measures rotation and acceleration), 1000 times a second.
  • 21 个关节电机，各自每秒 1000 次报告角度、速度和电流；两只手腕上各一个力传感器，也是每秒 1000 次。21 joint motors, each reporting its angle, speed and current 1000 times a second; and a force/torque sensor on each wrist, also 1000 times a second.

你说完那句话，前后十秒钟，它做了四件事：Once you have said it, the robot does four things in ten seconds:

  • ① 听（0 到 1.5 秒）
    麦克风把声音变成数；语音识别把它变成文字；一个大模型读懂这句话，想好要做什么。    ① Hear (0 to 1.5 seconds)
    The microphones turn the sound into numbers; speech recognition turns these into text; a large model reads and understands the sentence and works out what to do.
  • ② 看（1.5 到 3 秒）
    头部相机看台面，找出那杯水和你的手；任务被拆成几步：过去、抓起、递过来。    ② Look (1.5 to 3 seconds)
    The head camera looks at the worktop and finds the glass of water and your hand; the task is broken into steps: go there, pick it up, hand it over.
  • ③ 伸手（3 到 7 秒）
    一个"动作模型"每秒看十次相机和关节，每次交出接下来一秒的动作；下面一层层的控制环把动作变成 21 个电机里的电流。    ③ Reach (3 to 7 seconds)
    An "action model" looks at the cameras and joints ten times a second and each time hands over the actions for the next second; layer upon layer of control loops below it turn those actions into currents in the 21 motors.
  • ④ 递（7 到 10 秒）
    开到你面前伸出手；你一拉，手腕的力传感器几毫秒内就测到，夹爪松开。    ④ Hand over (7 to 10 seconds)
    It drives up to you and holds out its hand; as soon as you pull, the wrist force/torque sensor picks it up within a few milliseconds, and the gripper lets go.

第 5 篇把机器人要做的事分成六层：传感、感知与估计、决策、规划、控制、执行；还讲了它们怎样一级套一级地闭成快慢不同的环。这台机器人也是这六层，新的地方在于：有几层交给了大的神经网络。一个慢的规划模型，几十亿个参数，负责"听懂、找到、拆成几步"，有事才算，算一次要零点几秒；一个快的动作模型，也有几十亿个参数，每秒算十次，把"现在看到的"和"要做的"变成手臂接下来的动作。它们下面，还是第 5 篇那些不需要大模型的环：每毫秒一次的全身控制，每个关节里每秒两万次的电流环。这些事分在好几种芯片上：胸口一块主计算模块（里面有 CPU、GPU 和内存），一块专门对时间、收数据的芯片，21 块装在关节里的单片机，再加上相机、IMU 自己的芯片；有时候还要通过网络，问一问数据中心里更大的模型。Page 5 split what a robot has to do into six layers: sensing, perception and estimation, decision, planning, control and actuation; it also showed how they nest, one level inside the next, into loops running at different speeds. This robot has the same six layers; what is new is that some of them have been handed to large neural networks. A slow planner model with billions of parameters takes care of "understand, find, break into steps"; it runs only when something comes up, and each run takes a few tenths of a second. A fast action model, also with billions of parameters, runs ten times a second and turns "what it sees now" and "what it has to do" into the arms’ next movements. Below them are still the loops from page 5 that need no large model: whole-body control once every millisecond, and the current loop in each joint, 20,000 times a second. This work is spread over several kinds of chip: a main compute module in the chest (with a CPU, a GPU and memory inside), a chip dedicated to clock synchronisation and data collection, 21 microcontrollers inside the joints, plus the cameras’ and the IMU’s own chips; and sometimes the robot also goes over the network to ask a larger model in a data centre.

先玩：先在 ③ 上看 1 s：哪一行算得最少，哪一行最多，差了几倍？把放大镜一路调到 0.1 ms，看哪几行还在动。再跳到 ① 和 ②：规划模型什么时候开始算，算了多久？Try first: on ③, with the window at 1 s: which row runs least often, which most often, and by what factor? Take the window all the way down to 0.1 ms and see which rows are still moving. Then jump to ① and ②: when does the planner model start, and how long does it run for?

这十秒里已经藏着这一篇所有的问题。一秒钟里涌进来 163 MB 原始数据，99.7% 来自相机：它们先要有地方放，放在哪、放得下多少、读得多快，是存储的问题（第 ③ 步）。动作模型每秒算十次，每次是几万亿次乘法和加法（第 ④、⑦ 步）；规划模型一个词一个词地往外说，每说一个词，就要把几十亿个参数全读一遍，所以它快不快，看的不是芯片算得多快，而是内存搬得多快（第 ⑧ 步）。这类模型大多是在 NVIDIA 的 GPU 上训练的，靠的是一套叫 CUDA 的软件；也有不少在 Google 的 TPU 上训练，比如动作模型常用的底座 PaliGemma（Beyer 等 2024）（第 ⑥ 步）；训练它们的数据中心，要成千上万块 GPU、成千上万根光纤（第 ⑨ 步）。每秒 30 次的相机、每秒 1000 次的关节、每秒两万次的电流环，各在各的芯片上，各有各的钟，要对齐（第 ⑪ 步）；而这一切，都要装进一台靠电池跑的机器人里（第 ⑫、⑬ 步）。不过，要回答这些问题，先得知道芯片是什么。These ten seconds already hold every question on this page. In one second, 163 MB of raw data pours in, 99.7% of it from the cameras. First it needs somewhere to go: where it is kept, how much fits and how fast it can be read are questions of memory (step ③). The action model runs ten times a second, and each run is a few trillion multiplications and additions (steps ④ and ⑦). The planner model puts out its answer one token at a time, and for every token it has to read all of its billions of parameters, so how fast it goes depends not on how fast the chip computes but on how fast the memory moves data (step ⑧). Most models like these are trained on NVIDIA GPUs, relying on a set of software called CUDA; quite a few are trained on Google’s TPUs instead, such as PaliGemma, a common base for action models (Beyer et al. 2024) (step ⑥); the data centres that train them need thousands of GPUs and thousands of optical fibres (step ⑨). The cameras at 30 times a second, the joints at 1000 times a second and the current loops at 20,000 times a second each run on their own chips with their own clocks, and these have to be aligned (step ⑪); and all of this has to fit inside a robot that runs on a battery (steps ⑫ and ⑬). But to answer these questions, we first need to know what a chip is.

第 ① 步 · 芯片是什么Step ① · What a chip is

一块芯片，是几百亿个开关A chip is tens of billions of switches

机器人身上的芯片，长得都差不多：一片指甲盖大小、不到 1 毫米厚的硅片，封在一个小壳子里，焊在电路板上。硅片上刻着几百万到几千亿个晶体管。一个晶体管就是一个用电压控制的开关：它有三个端，控制端（栅极）上加了电压，另外两端之间就导通，电流能流过去；撤掉电压，就断开。导通和断开，就是 1 和 0。芯片做的每一件事，从加两个数，到让大模型说出一个词，都只是这些开关按某种次序一通一断。The chips on the robot all look much the same: a sliver of silicon the size of a fingernail and less than 1 mm thick, sealed in a small package and soldered onto a circuit board. Etched into the silicon are anywhere from a few million to a few hundred billion transistors. A transistor is a switch controlled by a voltage: it has three terminals, and when a voltage is applied to the control terminal (the gate), the other two are connected and current can flow between them; take the voltage away and the connection is broken. On and off are 1 and 0. Everything a chip does, from adding two numbers to making a large model say a word, is just these switches turning on and off in some order.

一个开关做不了什么，几个连起来就能做判断。四个晶体管能连成一个与非门（NAND）：两个输入都是 1 时输出 0，否则输出 1。用与非门可以拼出任何逻辑；几个门拼成一位加法器，算两位数字加上进位；32 个这样的加法器排成一串，就能加两个 32 位的数；很多加法器排成方阵，就是乘法器。存数也靠开关：6 个晶体管围成一个小圈（两个首尾相接的反相器，加两个开关），只要通着电，就能一直记住一个 0 或 1（MIT 6.004）。One switch cannot do much, but a few connected together can make decisions. Four transistors can be wired into a NAND gate: the output is 0 when both inputs are 1, and 1 otherwise. NAND gates can be combined into any logic at all; a few gates make a one-bit adder, which adds two binary digits plus a carry; 32 of these adders in a row add two 32-bit numbers; many adders laid out in a square grid make a multiplier. Storing a number also comes down to switches: 6 transistors form a small loop (two inverters, each feeding the other, plus two switches) that remembers a 0 or a 1 for as long as the power is on (MIT 6.004).

门和门之间靠导线连着，信号走过去要时间：电压要把下一级的一点点电容充满或放掉。为了让几十亿个门步调一致，芯片里有一个时钟：一个每秒跳几十亿下的方波。每跳一下，所有的寄存器（一排排能记住数的小格子）同时把上一段逻辑算出来的结果收进来，作为下一段的输入。两下之间，信号在逻辑里流动、稳定下来。时钟跳得多快，叫时钟频率，单位是赫兹（Hz）：主计算模块里的 CPU 和 GPU 每秒跳十几亿到几十亿下（GHz），关节里的单片机每秒一两亿下。Gates are joined by wires, and a signal takes time to travel along them: the voltage has to charge or drain a tiny amount of capacitance in the next stage. To keep billions of gates in step, a chip has a clock: a square wave that ticks billions of times a second. On every tick, all the registers (rows of little cells that can hold a number) take in, at the same instant, the results the previous stretch of logic has worked out, and these become the inputs to the next stretch. Between ticks, the signals flow through the logic and settle. How fast the clock ticks is the clock frequency, measured in hertz (Hz): the CPU and GPU in the main compute module tick from one to several billion times a second (GHz), and the microcontrollers in the joints one or two hundred million times a second.

fmax = 1 / tpathP ≈ α C V² f

时钟最快只能跳到"最长的一条路走完所需时间"的倒数。芯片每秒发的热（功率），大约等于：有多少比例的开关在翻转，乘上它们的电容，乘上电压的平方，再乘上时钟频率。The clock can tick no faster than one over "the time it takes to get through the longest path". The heat a chip gives off each second (its power) is roughly the fraction of switches that are flipping, times their capacitance, times the voltage squared, times the clock frequency.

两下时钟之间，最慢的那条信号路也必须走完，否则寄存器收进来的是半成品，所以频率被最长的路卡住；把一条长路切成几段、中间插寄存器（流水线），每一段变短，时钟就能跳得更快。每翻转一次，电源要给一点电容 C 充电，花掉的能量正比于 C V²；每秒翻转 α f 次，就是上面的功率。要让时钟更快，往往得把电压抬高，功率就涨得比频率快得多。2000 年代中期，CPU 的频率停在了每秒几十亿下，再没有大幅往上涨：不是做不到，而是芯片散不掉那么多热。以前晶体管每缩小一代，电压也跟着降，同样面积里的发热基本不变；到这时电压降不下去了（再降，漏电就太大），频率再往上抬，热就散不掉（National Research Council 2011）。从那以后，芯片变快主要靠"更多的单元同时算"，而不是"每个单元跳得更快"，这正是后面 GPU 胜出的原因。Between two ticks, even the slowest signal path has to finish, or the registers take in a half-finished result, so the frequency is held back by the longest path; cut a long path into several pieces with registers in between (a pipeline), and each piece is shorter, so the clock can tick faster. Every time a switch flips, the supply has to charge a little capacitance C, which costs energy proportional to C V²; with α f flips per second, that gives the power above. To make the clock faster you usually have to raise the voltage too, so the power grows much faster than the frequency. In the mid-2000s, CPU frequencies stalled at a few billion ticks a second and have not risen much since: not because it could not be done, but because the chips could not get rid of that much heat. Before then, each time transistors shrank by a generation the voltage came down with them, so the heat from a given area stayed about the same; by that point the voltage could not go any lower (any lower and the leakage would be too large), and pushing the frequency higher meant heat that could not be removed (National Research Council 2011). Since then, chips have got faster mainly through "more units computing at the same time" rather than "each unit ticking faster", and this is exactly why GPUs win out later on.

f, fmax
时钟频率和它能达到的最大值，Hz（每秒跳几下）；1 GHz 是每秒 109 下the clock frequency and the highest it can reach, Hz (ticks per second); 1 GHz is 109 ticks a second
tpath
两个寄存器之间最慢的那条逻辑路，从出发到稳定所需的时间（再加上寄存器自己收数的时间）the time the slowest logic path between two registers takes from start to settling (plus the time the register itself needs to take in the value)
P
动态功率，W：开关翻转消耗的那部分（还有一部分是漏电，不翻转也在耗）dynamic power, W: the part used up by switches flipping (another part is leakage, which goes on even when nothing flips)
α, C, V
每一下时钟里平均有多少比例的电路在翻转；这些电路的总电容，F（法拉）；电源电压，V（伏）the average fraction of the circuit that flips on each clock tick; the total capacitance of that circuit, F (farads); the supply voltage, V (volts)

假设最长的一条路要 350 ps（皮秒，10−12 秒）：fmax = 1 / 350 ps ≈ 2.86 GHz：时钟调到 2.9 GHz，就开始算错。光在 0.35 ns 里只走 10 厘米，信号在芯片的导线里走得更慢，所以芯片做得越大，最长的路也越难缩短。功率：电压从 0.8 V 抬到 1.0 V、频率从 2 GHz 抬到 3 GHz，功率变成原来的 (1.0/0.8)² × 1.5 ≈ 2.3 倍，速度却只快了 1.5 倍。Suppose the longest path takes 350 ps (picoseconds, 10−12 s): fmax = 1 / 350 ps ≈ 2.86 GHz, so with the clock set to 2.9 GHz the chip starts getting answers wrong. In 0.35 ns light travels only 10 cm, and signals in a chip’s wires travel more slowly still, so the bigger the chip, the harder it is to shorten its longest path. Power: raise the voltage from 0.8 V to 1.0 V and the frequency from 2 GHz to 3 GHz, and the power becomes (1.0/0.8)² × 1.5 ≈ 2.3 times what it was, while the speed is only 1.5 times higher.

"芯片多快"不只看频率：一下时钟里能做多少事同样重要。同样每秒跳 20 亿下，一个只做一次加法的单元，和一个每下做几千次乘加的单元，差了几千倍。"How fast is a chip?" is not just a question of frequency: how much it does in one clock tick matters just as much. At the same 2 billion ticks a second, a unit that does one addition per tick and a unit that does thousands of multiply–accumulates per tick differ by a factor of thousands.

芯片是怎么造出来的How chips are made

原料是提纯到极高纯度的硅，拉成一根圆柱，切成直径 300 mm 的薄圆片，叫晶圆。在晶圆上"印"电路，靠的是光刻：先涂一层遇光会变的胶，用光透过一张画着电路的掩模照上去，再把照过或没照过的地方刻掉、掺进别的原子、填上金属。一层叠一层，几十层下来，底下是晶体管，上面是十几层把它们连起来的铜导线。今天最细的那几层要用波长 13.5 nm 的极紫外光（EUV）来印。一片晶圆在工厂里要走几个月、上千道工序，最后切成几十片（像 B200 那样的大芯片）到几千片（小的单片机）裸片（die），每片封装好，就是一块芯片。The raw material is silicon refined to extremely high purity, grown into a cylinder and sliced into thin discs 300 mm across, called wafers. Circuits are "printed" onto a wafer by lithography: first the wafer is given a coating that changes when light falls on it, then light is shone through a mask with the circuit drawn on it, and then the parts that were (or were not) exposed are etched away, have other atoms mixed in or are filled with metal. Layer upon layer, dozens of them: the transistors at the bottom, and above them a dozen or so layers of copper wiring that connect them. Today the finest few layers have to be printed with extreme ultraviolet light (EUV) with a wavelength of 13.5 nm. A wafer spends months in the factory and goes through more than a thousand process steps; at the end it is cut into anything from a few dozen (for a big chip like the B200) to several thousand (for small microcontrollers) dies (bare chips), and each one, once packaged, is a chip.

常听到的"3 nm""2 nm"是工艺的代号，不是晶体管真有 3 纳米大；它大致表示又往前走了一代：同样的面积里能放更多的晶体管，同样的速度下更省电。数量上的变化很直观：1971 年的第一块商用微处理器 Intel 4004 只有约 2300 个晶体管，时钟每秒不到一百万下；2024 年 NVIDIA 的 B200 GPU 有 2080 亿个，分在两片裸片上。一片裸片能做多大也有上限：光刻机一次能照的面积大约是 26 mm × 33 mm，所以更大的芯片一般拆成几片，再在封装里拼起来（第 ⑭ 步）；Cerebras 把一整片晶圆做成一块芯片，是少见的例外（第 ⑥ 步）。The "3 nm" and "2 nm" you often hear about are names for process generations; the transistors are not really 3 nanometres in size. Roughly, each name means one more generation forward: more transistors in the same area, and less power at the same speed. The change in numbers speaks for itself: the first commercial microprocessor, the Intel 4004 of 1971, had only about 2300 transistors and a clock of under a million ticks a second; NVIDIA’s B200 GPU of 2024 has 208 billion, split across two dies. There is also a limit to how big one die can be: a lithography machine can expose an area of only about 26 mm × 33 mm at a time, so bigger chips are usually split into several dies that are joined up again in the package (step ⑭); Cerebras, which makes a whole wafer into a single chip, is a rare exception (step ⑥).

  • 按钮选一层看：开关、与非门、加法器、时钟。Use the buttons to choose a level to look at: Switch, NAND gate, Adder, Clock.
  • 开关：点栅极切换控制端的电压，看电流通不通。与非门：点 A、B 切换两个输入，亮的是正在导通的晶体管，右边的表标出现在是哪一行。Switch: press Gate to toggle the voltage on the control terminal and see whether current flows. NAND gate: press A and B to toggle the two inputs; the lit transistors are the ones conducting, and the table on the right marks the current row.
  • 加法器：点上面两行的格子设两个 4 位二进制数；一步一步让进位一级一级往左传。时钟：拖时钟频率，看最长的那条路来不来得及走完，功率怎么变。Adder: click the cells in the top two rows to set two 4-bit binary numbers; press Step by step to pass the carry left one stage at a time. Clock: drag Clock frequency to see whether the longest path finishes in time and how the power changes.

先玩：在与非门里，什么时候输出才是 0？在加法器里算 7 + 9：进位要走几级才停下？在时钟里把频率一路拖高：从哪一下开始，寄存器收进来的数错了？那时候功率是一开始的几倍？Try first: In the NAND gate, when is the output 0? In the adder, work out 7 + 9: through how many stages does the carry travel before it stops? In the clock, drag the frequency all the way up: at what point do the registers start taking in wrong numbers? By then, how many times the starting power is the chip using?

这一步的要点：芯片是刻在硅片上的几百万到几千亿个开关；开关拼成门，门拼成加法器和存数的格子；时钟让它们一步一步同步地走。频率被最长的一条路和发热卡住，所以芯片变快，主要靠让更多单元同时算。The point of this step: A chip is millions to hundreds of billions of switches etched into silicon; switches make gates, and gates make adders and cells that store numbers; the clock moves them all forward in step, one tick at a time. The frequency is held back by the longest path and by heat, so chips get faster mainly by having more units compute at once.

第 ② 步 · 程序怎么跑起来Step ② · How a program runs

从一行代码到一串指令From a line of code to a string of instructions

机器人的规划模型、动作模型、全身控制，都是程序。程序要变成芯片里开关的通断，中间隔着好几层。最底下一层是指令：芯片能直接执行的一个个小步骤，比如"把内存里这个地方的数取到寄存器 r1""r1 乘 r2，结果放进 r3""如果 r3 小于 0，跳到第 40 条"。一种芯片认得哪些指令，叫它的指令集：个人电脑和服务器多用 x86，手机、苹果电脑和机器人的主计算模块多用 Arm，还有开放的 RISC-V。The robot’s planning model, its action model and its whole-body control are all programs. Between a program and the switches turning on and off inside a chip there are several layers. The bottom layer is instructions: small steps the chip can carry out directly, such as "load the number at this address in memory into register r1", "multiply r1 by r2 and put the result in r3" or "if r3 is less than 0, jump to instruction 40". The instructions a kind of chip understands make up its instruction set: PCs and servers mostly use x86; phones, Macs and the robot’s main compute module mostly use Arm; and there is also the open RISC-V.

CPU（中央处理器）做的事，说起来只有一个循环：按"程序计数器"指的位置，从内存里取出下一条指令，译出它要做什么，执行（让运算单元算一下，或者读写一次内存），把结果写回寄存器，程序计数器往下挪一条，再来。现代 CPU 把这几步做成流水线，同时有好几条指令在不同的阶段里；还会猜下一步要跳到哪、把后面不相干的指令提前做，所以一下时钟平均能做完好几条指令。一个 CPU 芯片里有好几个到上百个这样的核，每个核能独立地跑一串指令。What a CPU (central processing unit) does comes down to a single loop: from the address the "program counter" points to, fetch the next instruction from memory, decode what it asks for, execute it (have the arithmetic unit compute something, or read or write memory once), write back the result into a register, move the program counter on by one, and go round again. A modern CPU turns these steps into a pipeline, so several instructions are at different stages at once; it also guesses where the program will jump next and does later, unrelated instructions ahead of time, so on average it finishes several instructions per clock tick. A CPU chip holds anywhere from a few to over a hundred such cores, and each core can run its own string of instructions independently.

T = Ninst × CPI / f

一个程序要跑多久，等于它要执行的指令条数，乘上平均每条指令要几下时钟，再除以时钟频率。The time a program takes equals the number of instructions it executes, times the average number of clock ticks per instruction, divided by the clock frequency.

这是计算机结构教科书里的"CPU 性能方程"。它把"快"拆成三件可以分开改的事：少做几条指令（用一条能顶几十条的指令，比如一次做一整排乘法的向量指令、一次做一小块矩阵乘法的张量指令）；每条指令少花几下时钟（流水线、一次发射好几条）；时钟跳快一点（第 ① 步说过，这条路差不多走到头了）。GPU 和各种专用芯片，基本都是在第一件事上做文章。This is the "CPU performance equation" of computer architecture textbooks. It splits "fast" into three things that can be improved separately: execute fewer instructions (use one instruction that does the work of dozens, such as a vector instruction that does a whole row of multiplications at once, or a tensor instruction that does a small block of matrix multiplication at once); spend fewer clock ticks on each instruction (pipelining, issuing several at a time); and tick the clock faster (as step ① said, that road has nearly run out). GPUs and accelerators of every kind work mostly on the first.

T
程序运行的时间，sthe time the program takes to run, s
Ninst
执行的指令条数the number of instructions executed
CPI
平均每条指令要几下时钟（cycles per instruction）；小于 1 说明一下时钟能做完不止一条the average number of clock ticks each instruction takes (cycles per instruction); below 1 means more than one instruction finishes per tick
f
时钟频率，Hzthe clock frequency, Hz

全身控制每毫秒要算一次。假设一次要执行 20 万条指令，CPU 核每秒跳 20 亿下、平均一下时钟做完 2 条（CPI = 0.5）：T = 2 × 105 × 0.5 / (2 × 109) = 50 µs，只占 1 毫秒的二十分之一，来得及。可动作模型算一次要约 2.4 万亿次乘加（第 ⑫ 步）：就算每条指令做 16 次乘加，一个核也要 2.4 × 1012 / 16 × 0.5 / (2 × 109) ≈ 38 s，可它每 0.1 秒就要算一次，所以不能交给 CPU 一条一条地做。Whole-body control has to run once every millisecond. Suppose one run executes 200,000 instructions, and the CPU core ticks 2 billion times a second and finishes 2 instructions per tick on average (CPI = 0.5): T = 2 × 105 × 0.5 / (2 × 109) = 50 µs, only a twentieth of 1 ms, so there is plenty of time. But one run of the action model takes about 2.4 trillion multiply–accumulates (step ⑫): even if each instruction did 16 of them, one core would need 2.4 × 1012 / 16 × 0.5 / (2 × 109) ≈ 38 s, and the model has to run every 0.1 s, so it cannot be left to a CPU working through one instruction after another.

指令不会自己从天上掉下来：写程序用的是 Python、C++ 这样的语言，由编译器翻译成指令（Python 是由一个叫解释器的程序边读边执行）。管着所有程序轮流用哪个核、用哪块内存的，是操作系统；和 GPU、网卡、相机这些设备打交道的，是叫驱动的小程序。Instructions do not fall from the sky: programs are written in languages such as Python and C++, which a compiler translates into instructions (Python is instead run by a program called an interpreter, which reads it and executes it as it goes). The operating system decides which program takes its turn on which core and which part of memory it uses; small programs called drivers deal with devices such as the GPU, the network card and the cameras.

大模型怎样"调用"GPUHow a large model "calls" the GPU

规划模型的程序是用 Python 写的，跑在 PyTorch 这样的框架上。它的核心是一句句矩阵乘法，比如 y = x @ W（输入向量乘以权重矩阵）。这一行代码，一层一层地往下走：Python 解释器在 CPU 上执行到这一行，交给 PyTorch；PyTorch 看到 x 和 W 都放在 GPU 上，就选 GPU 的实现，调用 NVIDIA 的矩阵乘法库 cuBLAS；cuBLAS 挑一个最适合这个大小的 GPU 程序（叫核函数，kernel），通过 CUDA 驱动把"去执行这个核函数"的命令放进一个队列，然后马上返回，CPU 接着往下走；GPU 从队列里取到命令，让几万个线程同时开算。算出来的 y 还留在 GPU 上，等着下一层用。The planning model’s program is written in Python and runs on a framework such as PyTorch. At its heart is one matrix multiplication after another, for example y = x @ W (the input vector times a weight matrix). This one line of code works its way down, layer by layer: the Python interpreter, running on the CPU, reaches the line and hands it to PyTorch; PyTorch sees that x and W are both on the GPU, so it picks the GPU implementation and calls cuBLAS, NVIDIA’s matrix-multiplication library; cuBLAS picks the GPU program best suited to this size (called a kernel) and, through the CUDA driver, puts the command "run this kernel" into a queue, then returns at once, and the CPU carries on; the GPU takes the command from the queue and sets tens of thousands of threads computing at the same time. The result, y, stays on the GPU, waiting for the next layer to use it.

这里有一个关键：GPU 只能算已经放在它自己内存里的数。CPU 旁边的内存（内存，RAM）和 GPU 自己的内存（显存，VRAM）是两块不同的芯片，中间隔着一条叫 PCIe 的线，它比显存本身慢几十倍：H100 SXM 的显存每秒 3.35 TB（NVIDIA），PCIe 5.0 的 16 条通道每个方向只有约 64 GB/s（NVIDIA 标的 128 GB/s 是两个方向加起来，NVIDIA 2022），差 50 多倍。所以模型的几十亿个参数要在开始时整个搬进显存，一直住在那里；每说一个词都要用到全部参数，要是每次都从内存隔着 PCIe 搬一遍，就慢得没法用。显存放不下模型，就只能切开放到几块 GPU 上，或者每次隔着 PCIe 现搬，慢得没法用：这就是为什么大模型要越来越大的显存。机器人的主计算模块（还有手机、苹果电脑）是另一种做法：CPU 和 GPU 做在同一块芯片上，共用同一块内存，不用来回搬；代价是这块内存比数据中心 GPU 的显存慢得多（第 ③ 步）。There is a key point here: a GPU can only compute on numbers that are already in its own memory. The memory beside the CPU (main memory, RAM) and the GPU’s own memory (GPU memory, VRAM) are separate chips with a link called PCIe between them, and that link is dozens of times slower than the GPU memory itself: an H100 SXM’s GPU memory moves 3.35 TB a second (NVIDIA), while 16 lanes of PCIe 5.0 manage only about 64 GB/s in each direction (the 128 GB/s NVIDIA quotes is both directions added together, NVIDIA 2022), a difference of more than 50 times. So the model’s billions of parameters have to be moved into GPU memory in one go at the start and stay there; every word it says uses all the parameters, and copying them over PCIe from main memory every time would be too slow to be of any use. If the model does not fit in GPU memory, it has to be split across several GPUs, or copied over PCIe on the fly every time, which is too slow to be of any use: this is why large models need ever larger GPU memory. The robot’s main compute module (and phones and Macs too) does it differently: the CPU and GPU are built on the same chip and share the same memory, so nothing has to be copied back and forth; the price is that this memory is much slower than the GPU memory of a data-centre GPU (step ③).

  • 按钮选CPU 执行指令或PyTorch 调用 GPU。Use the buttons to choose A CPU runs instructions or PyTorch calls the GPU.
  • CPU 执行指令：一个只有 4 个寄存器的玩具 CPU，跑一段算 y = w·x + b 的小程序（神经网络里最小的一块）。一步：走一下时钟，看取指、译码、执行、写回各在哪；跑完、重来。A CPU runs instructions: a toy CPU with only 4 registers runs a short program that computes y = w·x + b (the smallest piece of a neural network). Step ticks the clock once: see where fetch, decode, execute and write back each take place. There are also Run to the end and Reset.
  • PyTorch 调用 GPU：一边是 y = x @ W 往下走经过的每一层，另一边是 CPU 和 GPU 两条时间线（宽屏时左右并排，手机上上下排）。拖矩阵大小，看一次计算里有多少时间花在"发命令"上、多少花在 GPU 真算上；关掉权重留在显存里，看每次都从内存搬权重会慢多少。PyTorch calls the GPU: on one side, every layer that y = x @ W passes through on its way down; on the other, two timelines, one for the CPU and one for the GPU (side by side on a wide screen, one above the other on a phone). Drag Matrix size to see how much of one computation goes on "sending the command" and how much on the GPU actually computing; switch off Keep the weights in GPU memory to see how much slower it gets when the weights are copied from main memory every time.

先玩：让玩具 CPU 一步一步走完：一共用了几下时钟、几条指令？换到 PyTorch：矩阵很小时，时间主要花在哪？关掉"权重留在显存里"，一次计算慢了多少倍？Try first: Step the toy CPU all the way through: how many clock ticks and how many instructions did it take? Switch to PyTorch: when the matrix is small, where does most of the time go? Switch off "Keep the weights in GPU memory": how many times slower does one computation get?

这一步的要点：程序最后都变成一串指令；CPU 一条条地取、译、执行，一个核一下时钟做几条。大模型的程序从 Python 一层层往下，最后变成发给 GPU 的核函数，由几万个线程同时算；GPU 只算放在显存里的数，所以模型必须整个住在显存里。The point of this step: Every program ends up as a string of instructions; a CPU fetches, decodes and executes them one by one, and one core gets through a few per clock tick. A large model’s program goes down layer by layer from Python and ends up as kernels sent to the GPU, run by tens of thousands of threads at once; a GPU only computes on numbers in GPU memory, so the whole model has to live in GPU memory.

第 ③ 步 · 存储Step ③ · Memory

快的小，大的慢Fast is small, big is slow

还在厨房里打个比方。做菜时，手里拿着的那一样最顺手，但手里只拿得下一两样；台面上能摆十几样，伸手就到；冰箱里能放几百样，要走两步、开门找；地下室的储藏室什么都有，跑一趟要几分钟；再没有的，得去超市。芯片里的存储也是这样一层一层排开：越靠近运算单元的越快，也越小。Let’s stay in the kitchen for an analogy. When you cook, whatever is in your hand is the easiest to use, but you can only hold one or two things; the worktop holds a dozen or so, within arm’s reach; the fridge holds hundreds, but you have to take a couple of steps, open the door and look; the storeroom in the basement has everything, but a trip there takes a few minutes; for anything else, you have to go to the supermarket. A chip’s memory is laid out in levels in just the same way: the closer to the compute units, the faster, and the smaller.

  • 寄存器：运算单元"手里"的那几个数，一下时钟就能用上。CPU 的每个核几十到几百个；GPU 的每个 SM 有 65536 个（256 KB），一块 B200 合计约 39 MB。Registers: the few numbers the compute units hold "in their hands", ready to use within one clock tick. Each CPU core has tens to hundreds of them; each SM of a GPU has 65536 (256 KB), about 39 MB in all on a B200.
  • 缓存（SRAM，静态存储器）：做在同一片芯片上，每个比特要 6 个晶体管，所以又快又占地方，只有几 MB 到一百多 MB（B200 的二级缓存是 126 MB，Chips and Cheese 2025）。Cache (SRAM, static RAM): built on the same chip, at 6 transistors per bit, so it is fast but takes up a lot of room, and there is only a few MB to a little over a hundred MB of it (the B200’s L2 cache is 126 MB, Chips and Cheese 2025).
  • 内存（DRAM，动态存储器）：单独的芯片，每个比特只要 1 个晶体管加 1 个小电容，便宜、能做大，几十到几百 GB；电容会漏电，每隔几十毫秒要"刷新"一遍。按用途分好几种：电脑里的 DDR5，手机和机器人主计算模块里的 LPDDR5X（省电），显卡上的 GDDR7，数据中心 GPU 旁边的 HBM。Main memory (DRAM, dynamic RAM): separate chips, needing only 1 transistor and 1 tiny capacitor per bit, so it is cheap and can be made large, tens to hundreds of GB; the capacitors leak, so the contents have to be "refreshed" every few tens of milliseconds. There are several kinds for different uses: DDR5 in computers, LPDDR5X in phones and the robot’s main compute module (low power), GDDR7 on graphics cards, and HBM beside data-centre GPUs.
  • 闪存（固态硬盘，SSD）：断电也不丢，能做到几 TB，可读得慢得多。模型文件平时存在这里，开机时整个读进内存或显存。Flash (solid-state drives, SSD): keeps its contents with the power off and can hold several TB, but is much slower to read. Model files normally live here and are read in full into main memory or GPU memory at start-up.
  • 网络：别的机器上的存储，隔着网线或无线，最慢。Network: storage on other machines, reached over a cable or wirelessly; the slowest of all.

说一种存储，要看三个数：容量（放得下多少字节），带宽（每秒能搬多少字节），延迟（要一个数，从发出请求到它到手要多久）。三者常常此消彼长：容量越大的越慢、越远。对大模型来说，最要命的是带宽，下面这个式子说明为什么。Any kind of memory is described by three numbers: capacity (how many bytes it holds), bandwidth (how many bytes it can move per second) and latency (how long it takes from asking for a number to having it in hand). The three usually trade off against one another: the bigger the capacity, the slower and further away the memory. For large models, bandwidth is what matters most, and the formula below shows why.

tread = S / BWrtok ≤ BW / S

把模型的全部参数从某一层存储里读一遍，要花"参数占的字节数除以那一层的带宽"这么久。一个词一个词往外说的时候，每说一个词都要把全部参数读一遍，所以每秒最多说出"带宽除以模型字节数"这么多个词。Reading all of a model’s parameters once from a given level of memory takes "the bytes the parameters occupy divided by that level’s bandwidth". When the model is producing words one at a time, every word needs a full read of all the parameters, so at most it can say "bandwidth divided by model bytes" words a second.

大模型每生成一个词，要拿当前的向量去乘每一层的每一个权重矩阵（第 ⑦ 步），几十亿个参数一个不落；而运算单元只能算已经搬到它跟前的数。一个人用的时候，这些参数用一次就扔，下一个词又得重新搬一遍，所以速度被"搬"卡住，而不是被"算"卡住。好几个人同时用（一批），一次搬来的参数可以给大家共用，这个上限才被抬高（第 ⑦、⑧ 步）。For every word a large model generates, it has to multiply the current vector by every weight matrix in every layer (step ⑦), all of its billions of parameters without exception; and the compute units can only work on numbers that have already been brought to them. With a single user, the parameters are used once and thrown away, and for the next word they all have to be moved in again, so the speed is limited by "moving", not by "computing". Only when several people use it at once (a batch) can the parameters brought in on one trip be shared by everyone, which raises this ceiling (steps ⑦ and ⑧).

S
模型参数占的字节数：参数个数 × 每个参数几字节（16 位的 BF16 是 2 字节，8 位的 FP8 是 1 字节，4 位是 0.5 字节）the bytes the model’s parameters occupy: number of parameters × bytes per parameter (16-bit BF16 is 2 bytes, 8-bit FP8 is 1 byte, 4-bit is 0.5 bytes)
BW
存储的带宽，字节/秒（GB/s，TB/s）the bandwidth of the memory, bytes per second (GB/s, TB/s)
tread
把参数从这一层读一遍的时间，sthe time to read the parameters once from this level, s
rtok
一个人用的时候，每秒最多生成几个词（词元，第 ⑦ 步再细说）the most words (tokens; more on these in step ⑦) that can be generated per second with a single user

机器人的规划模型有 80 亿个参数，用 FP8 存，S = 8 GB。放在机器人主计算模块的内存里（LPDDR5X，带宽 273 GB/s，NVIDIA 2026）：读一遍要 8 / 273 ≈ 29 ms，每秒最多说 34 个词。同一个模型放在数据中心一块 B200 GPU 的显存里（HBM3E，约 8 TB/s，NVIDIA）：读一遍 1 ms，每秒最多 1000 个词。放在一块 PCIe 4.0 的固态硬盘里（每秒约 7.45 GB，Samsung）：读一遍要 1.1 秒，一秒钟说不出一个词；最快的 PCIe 5.0 固态硬盘快一倍（Tom’s Hardware 2025），也只有每秒 2 个词上下。The robot’s planning model has 8 billion parameters stored in FP8, so S = 8 GB. In the memory of the robot’s main compute module (LPDDR5X, bandwidth 273 GB/s, NVIDIA 2026), one read takes 8 / 273 ≈ 29 ms, so it can say at most 34 words a second. The same model in the GPU memory of one B200 in a data centre (HBM3E, about 8 TB/s, NVIDIA): one read takes 1 ms, at most 1000 words a second. On a PCIe 4.0 SSD (about 7.45 GB a second, Samsung): one read takes 1.1 s, so it cannot manage even one word a second; the fastest PCIe 5.0 SSDs are twice as fast (Tom’s Hardware 2025), which still means only about 2 words a second.

这就回答了"为什么要更大的显存"：放不下，就只能把模型切开放在好几块 GPU 上（第 ⑧、⑨ 步），或者用更少的位数存每个参数；也回答了"为什么要更快的显存"：在一个人用的时候，生成速度几乎完全由带宽决定。This answers "why do we need bigger GPU memory?": if the model does not fit, it has to be split across several GPUs (steps ⑧ and ⑨), or each parameter has to be stored in fewer bits. It also answers "why do we need faster GPU memory?": with a single user, generation speed is set almost entirely by bandwidth.

HBM：把内存叠起来，贴在 GPU 旁边HBM: memory stacked up and placed right next to the GPU

数据中心的 GPU 用的显存叫 HBM（高带宽内存）。它把 8 到 16 片 DRAM 裸片一片片叠起来，用垂直穿过硅片的细铜柱（硅通孔，TSV）连通，底下垫一片管理用的逻辑芯片；这样一摞，再和 GPU 一起放在一片硅中介层上，彼此只隔几毫米，用上千根并排的线连接（HBM3E 每摞 1024 根数据线，HBM4 是 2048 根）。线多、线短，带宽就大：一块 B200 旁边放了好几摞，一共约 180 GB、约 8 TB/s（DGX B200 的 8 块合计 1440 GB、64 TB/s，NVIDIA；单卖的 180 GB 版本标 7.7 TB/s，Lenovo 2025）。代价是贵，产量受限，容量也比不上普通内存条。The GPU memory of data-centre GPUs is called HBM (high-bandwidth memory). It stacks 8 to 16 DRAM dies one on top of another, connects them with thin copper pillars running vertically through the silicon (through-silicon vias, TSVs), and puts a logic die underneath to manage them; each stack then sits with the GPU on a silicon interposer, only a few millimetres apart, connected by more than a thousand wires side by side (1024 data wires per stack for HBM3E, 2048 for HBM4). Many wires and short wires mean high bandwidth: a B200 has several stacks beside it, about 180 GB and about 8 TB/s in total (1440 GB and 64 TB/s for the 8 GPUs of a DGX B200 together, NVIDIA; the 180 GB version sold on its own is rated at 7.7 TB/s, Lenovo 2025). The price: it is expensive, supply is limited, and its capacity cannot match ordinary memory modules.

机器人的主计算模块走的是另一条路：CPU 和 GPU 做在一块芯片上，共用 128 GB 的 LPDDR5X。容量够放好几个模型，可带宽只有 B200 的约三十分之一。手机、苹果电脑也是这种做法：省电、便宜、不用来回搬，但带宽是它的天花板。The robot’s main compute module takes another road: the CPU and GPU are on one chip and share 128 GB of LPDDR5X. That is enough capacity for several models, but the bandwidth is only about a thirtieth of a B200’s. Phones and Macs do the same: low power, cheap, nothing to copy back and forth, but bandwidth is the ceiling.

Ppeak ∝ 3.0t / 2BWmem ∝ 1.6t / 2BWlink ∝ 1.4t / 2

过去二十年，服务器芯片的峰值算力每两年涨到约 3 倍；内存带宽每两年只涨到约 1.6 倍；芯片之间的连线带宽每两年约 1.4 倍（Gholami 等 2024）。Over the past twenty years, the peak compute of server chips has grown about 3-fold every two years; memory bandwidth only about 1.6-fold every two years; and the bandwidth of the links between chips about 1.4-fold every two years (Gholami et al. 2024).

运算单元可以靠更小的晶体管、更多的单元、更少的位数一起往上堆；内存带宽受限于芯片边上能引出多少根线、每根线能跑多快、跑一个比特要花多少能量，这几样都涨得慢。差距一年年拉大，叫内存墙（这个词出自 Wulf & McKee 1995）：越来越多的时候，芯片不是在算，而是在等数据。HBM 一层层往上叠、线一代代加宽，就是在拆这堵墙。Compute can be piled up with smaller transistors, more units and fewer bits, all at once; memory bandwidth is limited by how many wires can be brought out at the edge of a chip, how fast each wire can run and how much energy it takes to send one bit, and all of these improve slowly. The gap widens year by year and is called the memory wall (the term comes from Wulf & McKee 1995): more and more of the time, a chip is not computing but waiting for data. Stacking HBM ever higher and making its interface wider with each generation are ways of tearing this wall down.

t
经过的年数the number of years that have passed
Ppeak
芯片的峰值算力，FLOPSthe chip’s peak compute, FLOPS
BWmem, BWlink
内存的带宽；芯片之间连线的带宽，字节/秒the memory bandwidth; the bandwidth of the links between chips, bytes per second
∝
"正比于"：只比增长的倍数，不管起点"is proportional to": compares only how many times something grows, not where it starts

十年是 t / 2 = 5 个"两年"：算力涨到 3.05 ≈ 243 倍，内存带宽只涨到 1.65 ≈ 10 倍，连线 1.45 ≈ 5.4 倍。Gholami 等统计的过去 20 年：峰值算力涨了约 6 万倍，内存带宽约 100 倍，连线约 30 倍。Ten years is t / 2 = 5 "two-year" periods: compute grows 3.05 ≈ 243-fold, memory bandwidth only 1.65 ≈ 10-fold, and links 1.45 ≈ 5.4-fold. Over the past 20 years, as counted by Gholami et al., peak compute grew about 60,000-fold, memory bandwidth about 100-fold and links about 30-fold.

这堵墙决定了很多事：为什么 GPU 要把存储做得离运算单元越来越近，为什么数字格式要越来越短（同样的带宽能多搬一倍的数），为什么有人想干脆在存储里算（第 ⑮ 步）。This wall explains a lot: why GPUs keep bringing memory closer to the compute units, why number formats keep getting shorter (the same bandwidth then moves twice as many numbers), and why some people want to compute right inside the memory (step ⑮).

  • 上面是存储的梯子：从寄存器到网络，每一层的容量和带宽（对数刻度：每一格是前一格的 10 倍），旁边写着延迟。At the top is the memory ladder: from registers to the network, each level’s capacity and bandwidth (log scale: each grid line is 10 times the one before), with its latency written beside it.
  • 按钮选一个模型（3B 是机器人的动作模型，8B 是它的规划模型，还有 70B、405B）和每个参数用几位存（BF16、FP8、FP4）：看它放得进哪几层，从每一层读一遍要多久，一个人用时每秒最多生成几个词。Use the buttons to choose a model (3B is the robot’s action model, 8B its planning model, plus 70B and 405B) and how many bits each parameter is stored in (BF16, FP8, FP4): see which levels it fits in, how long one read from each level takes, and the most words a second it can generate for a single user.
  • 换成人的尺度：把 1 纳秒放大成 1 秒，看看每一层的延迟相当于多久。Switch to human scale: stretch 1 nanosecond to 1 second and see what each level’s latency comes to.

先玩：选 8B、FP8：它放得进机器人的内存吗？每秒最多说几个词？换成 70B 呢？再打开"人的尺度"：从内存取一个数，相当于等多久？Try first: Choose 8B and FP8: does it fit in the robot’s memory? How many words a second can it say at most? What about 70B? Then press "Switch to human scale": on that scale, how long do you wait for one number from main memory?

这一步的要点：存储一层层排开，越近越快越小。大模型每生成一个词都要把全部参数读一遍，所以生成速度的上限是"带宽 ÷ 模型字节数"；模型得整个放进最快的那一层，放不下就要切开。运算涨得比带宽快，这堵内存墙是今天芯片设计的中心问题。The point of this step: Memory is laid out in levels, and the closer it is, the faster and smaller. A large model reads all its parameters for every word it generates, so generation speed is capped at "bandwidth ÷ model bytes"; the whole model has to fit in the fastest level, and if it does not fit it has to be split. Compute grows faster than bandwidth, and this memory wall is the central problem of chip design today.

第 ④ 步 · 算一次和搬一次Step ④ · Computing and moving data

算很便宜，搬很贵Computing is cheap, moving is expensive

神经网络里几乎全部的计算，都是同一个动作：拿一个权重乘一个输入，加到累计的和上。这叫乘加（multiply–accumulate，MAC）。一层神经网络 y = W x，权重矩阵 W 有 m 行、n 列，就要 m × n 次乘加。一次乘加算两次浮点运算（一次乘、一次加），所以常说"这层要 2mn 个 FLOP"。芯片每秒能做多少次，叫它的算力，单位 FLOPS；1 TFLOPS 是每秒 1012 次，1 PFLOPS 是每秒 1015 次。整数运算常用 TOPS（每秒万亿次运算）。Almost all the computation in a neural network is the same action: multiply a weight by an input and add the result to a running sum. This is called a multiply–accumulate (MAC). A neural-network layer y = W x with a weight matrix W of m rows and n columns needs m × n multiply–accumulates. One multiply–accumulate counts as two floating-point operations (one multiplication and one addition), which is why people say "this layer takes 2mn FLOP". How many of these operations a chip can do per second is called its compute, measured in FLOPS; 1 TFLOPS is 1012 a second and 1 PFLOPS is 1015 a second. For integer arithmetic, TOPS (trillions of operations per second) is the usual unit.

一个数用几位来存How many bits a number gets

浮点数像科学计数法：一位符号，几位指数（数量级），几位尾数（有效数字）。训练神经网络传统上用 32 位（FP32：1 + 8 + 23）；后来发现 16 位就够，BF16（1 + 8 + 7）保留了 FP32 的数量级范围，只砍掉尾数；推理时再降到 8 位（FP8，比如 1 + 4 + 3），最新的 GPU 已经能直接算 4 位（FP4：1 + 2 + 1）。4 位只能表示十几个值，所以每一小块数（比如 16 或 32 个）再共用一个缩放系数，让这十几个值落在合适的范围里。A floating-point number works like scientific notation: one bit for the sign, a few for the exponent (the order of magnitude) and a few for the mantissa (the significant digits). Neural networks were traditionally trained in 32 bits (FP32: 1 + 8 + 23). Then it turned out that 16 bits were enough: BF16 (1 + 8 + 7) keeps FP32’s range of magnitudes and cuts only the mantissa. For inference it drops again to 8 bits (FP8, for example 1 + 4 + 3), and the newest GPUs can compute directly in 4 bits (FP4: 1 + 2 + 1). With 4 bits there are only a dozen or so values, so each small block of numbers (say 16 or 32 of them) also shares one scale factor, so that those few values land in the right range.

位数减半有两个好处。一是数据少一半：同样的带宽每秒能多搬一倍的参数，同样的显存能多放一倍。二是乘法器小得多：一个乘法器的大小大致和尾数位数的平方成正比，同一片芯片能多放很多个，所以每降一级精度，GPU 标出来的算力往往翻一倍。代价是精度：π 用 FP4 存，只剩下 3。Halving the number of bits helps in two ways. First, there is half as much data: the same bandwidth moves twice as many parameters a second, and the same GPU memory holds twice as many. Second, the multipliers are much smaller: a multiplier’s size is roughly proportional to the square of the number of mantissa bits, so many more fit on the same chip, which is why each step down in precision often doubles the compute a GPU is rated at. The price is precision: π stored in FP4 is left as just 3.

E ≈ Nop · eop + Nbit · ebit

一次计算花的能量，大约等于"算了多少次"乘"每算一次花多少"，加上"搬了多少比特"乘"每搬一个比特花多少"。The energy a computation uses is roughly "how many operations" times "how much each operation costs", plus "how many bits are moved" times "how much moving each bit costs".

把两项分开看，就知道钱花在哪。Horowitz 2014 年在国际固态电路会议的主题报告里专门讲过这件事（Horowitz 2014）；常被引用的那张 45 nm 工艺的表是：32 位整数加法 0.1 pJ，32 位浮点乘法 3.7 pJ，从片上 SRAM 缓存读一个 32 位数 5 pJ，从片外 DRAM 读一个 32 位数 640 pJ（Han 等 2015）。从片外内存搬一个数，比拿它做一次浮点乘法贵 170 多倍，比一次整数加法贵 6400 倍。导线越长、要充放电的电容越大，搬起来越费电，这是物理，不是设计得不好。Keep the two terms apart and you can see where the energy goes. Horowitz made exactly this point in his 2014 keynote at the International Solid-State Circuits Conference (Horowitz 2014); the often-quoted 45 nm table reads: 32-bit integer add 0.1 pJ, 32-bit floating-point multiply 3.7 pJ, reading a 32-bit number from the on-chip SRAM cache 5 pJ, reading a 32-bit number from off-chip DRAM 640 pJ (Han et al. 2015). Fetching a number from off-chip memory costs over 170 times as much as doing one floating-point multiply with it, and 6400 times as much as an integer add. The longer the wire and the more capacitance there is to charge and discharge, the more energy a move takes: that is physics, not bad design.

E
一次计算消耗的能量，Jthe energy one computation uses, J
Nop, eop
运算次数；每次运算的能量，pJthe number of operations; the energy per operation, pJ
Nbit, ebit
从某一层存储搬过来的比特数；每搬一个比特的能量，pJ/bit（离运算单元越远越大）the number of bits moved in from a given level of memory; the energy to move one bit, pJ/bit (larger the further that level is from the arithmetic units)

规划模型（8B，FP8）在机器人上生成一个词，按这张 45 nm 的老表粗算。算：约 8 × 109 次乘加，就算每次按 16 位整数的乘法加加法 0.62 + 0.18 = 0.8 pJ（Pedram 等 2016），也只有约 6.4 mJ。搬：8 GB 参数从 DRAM 读一遍是 6.4 × 1010 个比特，按 640 pJ / 32 位 = 20 pJ 每比特，约 1.3 J。搬的是算的约 200 倍。今天的工艺下两项都小得多，但比例相近：一篇综述给的相对值是：从 DRAM 取一个数，能量约等于做 200 次乘加（Sze 等 2017）。Take the planner (8B, FP8) generating one token on the robot, and work it out roughly with this old 45 nm table. Compute: about 8 × 109 multiply–accumulates; even counting each as a 16-bit integer multiply plus an add, 0.62 + 0.18 = 0.8 pJ (Pedram et al. 2016), that is only about 6.4 mJ. Move: reading the 8 GB of parameters once from DRAM is 6.4 × 1010 bits; at 640 pJ / 32 bits = 20 pJ per bit, that is about 1.3 J. Moving takes about 200 times as much energy as computing. With today’s processes both terms are much smaller, but the ratio is similar; one survey gives the relative figure: fetching a number from DRAM costs about as much energy as 200 multiply–accumulates (Sze et al. 2017).

所以芯片设计的头号原则是：一个数搬到跟前，就尽量多用几次。把矩阵切成小块放进片上存储反复用、把很多人的请求凑成一批共用同一份权重、用更少的位数存，都是在减第二项。So the first rule of chip design is: once a number has been brought close, use it as many times as you can. Cutting matrices into small tiles that stay in on-chip memory and get reused, batching many people’s requests so that they share the same weights, storing numbers in fewer bits: all of these shrink the second term.

  • 最上面是每种操作花的能量（Horowitz 2014，45 nm 工艺），对数刻度：每一格是前一格的 10 倍。At the top is the energy of each operation (Horowitz 2014, 45 nm process), on a log scale: each gridline is 10 times the one before.
  • 中间是几种数字格式：按钮选 FP32、BF16、FP16、FP8、FP4，看同一个数用它存成什么样、差了多少，以及符号、指数、尾数各占几位。In the middle are the number formats: pick FP32, BF16, FP16, FP8 or FP4 with the buttons and see what the same number turns into when stored in it, how far off it is, and how many bits the sign, the exponent and the mantissa each get.
  • 最下面算一笔账：选一个模型和精度，看生成一个词时，"算"和"搬"各花多少能量。At the bottom is the bill: choose a model and a precision and see how much energy "compute" and "move" each take to generate one token.

先玩：从 DRAM 读一次，相当于做多少次 16 位的乘法？π 用 FP8 存成了多少？FP4 呢？在最下面选 8B、FP8：搬的能量是算的几倍？Try first: one read from DRAM is worth how many 16-bit multiplies? What does π become when stored in FP8? And in FP4? At the bottom, choose 8B and FP8: moving takes how many times the energy of computing?

这一步的要点：神经网络的计算几乎全是乘加；数用的位数越少，搬得越快、乘得越便宜，但越不准。真正花能量的不是乘法，而是把数从远处搬过来，所以芯片的设计都在想办法让一个数搬来以后多用几次。The point of this step: almost all the computation in a neural network is multiply–accumulates; the fewer bits a number uses, the faster it moves and the cheaper it is to multiply, but the less accurate it is. What really costs energy is not the multiplying but bringing numbers in from far away, so chip design is all about using a number many times once it has been brought in.

第 ⑤ 步 · 几类芯片Step ⑤ · Kinds of chip

同样的晶体管，不同的分法The same transistors, divided up differently

CPU、GPU、专用芯片、FPGA、单片机，都是用同样的晶体管做的。区别在于一片硅上的面积和电，花在哪：花在"决定下一步做什么"（控制），花在"算"（运算单元），还是花在"记"（存储）。花法不同，擅长的事就不同。CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, FPGAs and microcontrollers are all made of the same transistors. The difference is where a piece of silicon spends its area and its power: on "deciding what to do next" (control), on "computing" (arithmetic units) or on "remembering" (memory). Spend them differently and the chip is good at different things.

  • CPU：几个到上百个大核，大部分面积给了控制和缓存：猜分支、乱序执行、大缓存，为的是让一串前后依赖、到处跳转的指令尽快跑完。它最灵活，跑一串前后依赖的指令时延迟低，但每瓦能做的乘加比 GPU、专用芯片少得多。机器人里，操作系统、ROS 2 的程序、任务的逻辑、每毫秒一次的全身控制，跑在 CPU 上。CPU: anything from a few to over a hundred big cores, with most of the area given to control and cache: branch prediction, out-of-order execution and big caches, all so that a string of instructions that depend on one another and jump all over the place finishes as fast as possible. It is the most flexible and has low latency on a chain of dependent instructions, but it does far fewer multiply–accumulates per watt than a GPU or an accelerator. In the robot, the operating system, the ROS 2 programs, the task logic and the whole-body control (once every millisecond) run on the CPU.
  • GPU：本来是画画面的：屏幕上几百万个像素，每个都要按同样的公式算一遍颜色。所以它有上万个简单的运算单元，几十个一组听同一条指令，各算各的数据；再加上专门做小块矩阵乘法的张量核心，和旁边带宽极大的显存。它不擅长"一个接一个"的事，擅长"同样的事做一万遍"：神经网络正是这样。GPU: originally made for drawing the picture: millions of pixels on a screen, each needing its colour worked out with the same formula. So it has more than ten thousand simple arithmetic units, in groups of a few dozen that follow the same instruction while each works on its own data, plus tensor cores made just for small matrix multiplications, and GPU memory beside it with enormous bandwidth. It is poor at things done "one after another" and good at "the same thing ten thousand times": exactly what a neural network is.
  • 专用芯片（ASIC）：只为一类计算设计，常见的是脉动阵列：几千到几万个乘加单元排成方阵，数据像心跳一样一拍一拍地从边上流进去、在单元之间传递，一个数被拿来就在阵列里用上几百次，不用回内存。几乎没有控制逻辑，所以同样的面积和电能做最多的乘加。Google 的 TPU、手机里的神经网络处理器（NPU）、一些汽车的自动驾驶芯片都是这一类。缺点是不灵活：设计一款要几年，算法变了它可能就用不上。Accelerator (ASIC): designed for one kind of computation only. A common design is the systolic array: thousands to tens of thousands of multiply–accumulate units laid out in a square grid; data flow in from the edges beat by beat, like a heartbeat, and pass from unit to unit, so a number, once fetched, is used hundreds of times inside the array without going back to memory. There is almost no control logic, so the same area and power deliver the most multiply–accumulates. Google’s TPU, the neural processing units (NPUs) in phones and the self-driving chips in some cars are all of this kind. The drawback is inflexibility: one takes years to design, and if the algorithm changes it may no longer be any use.
  • FPGA（现场可编程门阵列）：一片芯片上铺满了小的查找表、触发器、乘法块和可以重新接线的开关，出厂以后，你还能把它"接"成自己想要的电路。它的时钟慢（几百 MHz），同样的事比专用芯片费电，可它延迟极低、每一拍做什么完全确定，还能接各种奇怪的接口。机器人里常用它管传感器：同时触发几台相机、给每个数据打上同一个钟的时间戳。FPGA (field-programmable gate array): a chip covered in small look-up tables, flip-flops, multiplier blocks and switches that can be rewired, so that even after it leaves the factory you can "wire" it into whatever circuit you want. Its clock is slow (a few hundred MHz) and it uses more power than an accelerator for the same job, but its latency is extremely low, what it does in every clock cycle is completely fixed, and it can connect to all kinds of odd interfaces. Robots often use one to manage sensors: triggering several cameras at once and stamping every piece of data with a timestamp from the same clock.
  • 单片机（MCU）：一个小 CPU 核，加上内存、闪存、定时器、模数转换器、PWM 输出，全做在一片几块钱的芯片上，功耗只有几十毫瓦到一两瓦。它的本事是准时：比如 Cortex-M4 这类单片机，中断信号一来，12 个时钟周期后就开始执行处理程序（存储器不插等待周期时），每次都一样（Yiu 2016），按 170 MHz 算约 70 纳秒。每个关节里每秒两万次的电流环（第 5 篇第 ⑤ 步），就跑在它上面。Microcontroller (MCU): a small CPU core plus RAM, flash, timers, analogue-to-digital converters and PWM outputs, all on one chip that costs a few dollars and draws only tens of milliwatts to a watt or two. Its strength is punctuality: on a Cortex-M4-class microcontroller, for example, the interrupt handler starts 12 clock cycles after the interrupt signal arrives (when the memory needs no wait states), the same every time (Yiu 2016): about 70 nanoseconds at 170 MHz. Each joint’s current loop, 20,000 times a second (page 5, step ⑤), runs on one of these.
  • 还有几种专门的：DSP（数字信号处理器）擅长滤波这类一串串的乘加；ISP（图像信号处理器）把相机传感器出来的原始数据变成一张正常的照片（插值出颜色、调白平衡、去噪）。And a few specialised ones: a DSP (digital signal processor) is good at long strings of multiply–accumulates such as filtering; an ISP (image signal processor) turns the raw data from a camera sensor into a normal photo (interpolating the colours, setting the white balance, removing noise).

传感器里也有芯片，但它们不是用来"算"的。比如 IMU：里面是一片用微加工刻出来的硅，上面有挂在细梁上的小质量块（MEMS，微机电系统），机器人一转、一加速，质量块就偏一点，电容跟着变；旁边另一片芯片把这一点点电容的变化放大、变成数字、滤波，再通过 SPI 这样的接口每秒送出上千次。所以 IMU 是传感器，不是计算单元，只是里面带着一块小小的读出芯片。相机也是：一片几百万个像素的感光芯片，每个像素把光变成电荷，再由芯片上的模数转换器变成数。Sensors have chips in them too, but these are not there to "compute". Take the IMU: inside is a piece of micromachined silicon with tiny masses hanging on thin beams (MEMS, micro-electromechanical systems). When the robot turns or accelerates, the masses shift slightly and a capacitance changes with them; another chip beside it amplifies this tiny change in capacitance, digitises it, filters it and sends it out over an interface such as SPI more than a thousand times a second. So an IMU is a sensor, not a computing unit; it just carries a small readout chip inside. A camera is the same: an image-sensor chip with millions of pixels, each turning light into charge, which an analogue-to-digital converter on the chip then turns into numbers.

最后，很多芯片会被做进同一片硅里，叫片上系统（SoC）。机器人的主计算模块就是一个 SoC：CPU 核、GPU、ISP、视频编解码器、内存控制器、各种接口都在一块芯片上，共用一组内存。手机芯片也是这样。Finally, many of these chips can be built into one piece of silicon, called a system on chip (SoC). The robot’s main compute module is an SoC: CPU cores, GPU, ISP, video codecs, memory controller and all kinds of interfaces sit on one chip and share one pool of memory. Phone chips are built the same way.

S = 1 / ((1 − p) + p / s)

一项工作里，有比例 p 的部分被加速了 s 倍，剩下的没变，整件事只快了 S 倍。If a fraction p of a job is sped up s times and the rest stays the same, the whole job is only S times faster.

这是 Amdahl 1967 年说的道理：被加速的那部分越快，没被加速的那部分就越显眼，最后整件事的速度被它卡住。所以专用芯片再快，也离不开一个 CPU 去处理那些它不会做的、一步接一步的事；一台好的计算机，是好几种芯片各干自己最擅长的那一份。This is the argument Amdahl made in 1967: the faster the accelerated part becomes, the more the part that was not accelerated stands out, until in the end it caps the speed of the whole job. So however fast an accelerator is, it still needs a CPU for the step-by-step work it is unable to do; a good computer is several kinds of chip, each doing the share it does best.

p
能被加速的部分占原来总时间的比例the fraction of the original total time spent on the part that can be sped up
s
那一部分被加速的倍数how many times faster that part becomes
S
整件事的加速倍数how many times faster the whole job becomes

动作模型算一次，95% 的时间是矩阵乘法，5% 是准备输入、整理输出这些零碎事。把矩阵乘法交给 GPU、快了 100 倍：S = 1 / (0.05 + 0.95/100) ≈ 16.8 倍，不是 100 倍。剩下那 5% 不处理好，再快的 GPU 也白搭。In one run of the action model, 95% of the time goes on matrix multiplication and 5% on odd jobs such as preparing the inputs and tidying up the outputs. Hand the matrix multiplication to a GPU that does it 100 times faster: S = 1 / (0.05 + 0.95/100) ≈ 16.8 times, not 100. If that remaining 5% is not dealt with, even the fastest GPU is wasted.

"哪种芯片最好"没有答案，只有"这件事交给谁最合适"。越灵活的越费电，越省电的越死板；机器人里每一层、每一级环，都在这条线上找自己的位置（第 ⑬ 步）。There is no answer to "which chip is best", only to "which chip suits this job best". The more flexible a chip, the more power it uses; the more frugal, the more rigid. In the robot, every layer and every level of loop finds its own place along this line (step ⑬).

  • 同一件事，交给五种芯片：算两个 8 × 8 矩阵的乘积，一共 512 次乘加。按钮选 CPU、GPU、脉动阵列、FPGA、单片机；播放或一步，看它们一拍一拍怎么算。The same job, handed to five kinds of chip: multiplying two 8 × 8 matrices, 512 multiply–accumulates in all. Pick CPU, GPU, Systolic array, FPGA or MCU with the buttons; press Play or Step to watch how each one computes, cycle by cycle.
  • 下面写着用了几拍、同时有几个单元在算、有多少单元闲着，以及它灵不灵活、每一拍做什么是否确定。Underneath are the cycles used, how many units are computing at once and how many are idle, and whether the chip is flexible and whether what it does in every cycle is fixed.
  • 换成很多 if 的代码：同样五种芯片，去跑一段到处分支的程序。Switch to code with lots of ifs: the same five chips run a program that branches everywhere.

先玩：先看脉动阵列：数据从哪边进、要几拍才算完？比一比 CPU 用了几拍。再换成"很多 if 的代码"：哪几种芯片还做得好？Try first: start with the systolic array: where does the data come in from, and how many cycles does it take to finish? Compare how many cycles the CPU uses. Then switch to "code with lots of ifs": which chips still do well?

这一步的要点：各种芯片的区别，是把晶体管花在控制、运算还是存储上：CPU 灵活、延迟低；GPU 让成千上万个单元做同样的事；专用芯片最省电、最死板；FPGA 能重新接线、时间最准；单片机便宜、准时。传感器里的芯片负责把物理量变成数。一台机器人要好几种一起用。The point of this step: chips differ in whether they spend their transistors on control, arithmetic or memory: the CPU is flexible and has low latency; the GPU sets thousands upon thousands of units doing the same thing; the accelerator is the most frugal and the most rigid; the FPGA can be rewired and keeps the most exact time; the microcontroller is cheap and punctual. The chips in sensors turn physical quantities into numbers. A robot needs several kinds working together.

第 ⑥ 步 · GPU 和 CUDAStep ⑥ · GPUs and CUDA

CUDA 是什么，为什么大多数人选 NVIDIA，还有哪些别的路What CUDA is, why most people choose NVIDIA, and what other routes there are

2000 年代初，显卡已经能按程序给每个像素算颜色了。有研究者发现：要是把一个大数组伪装成一张图片，把计算伪装成"给像素上色"，显卡就能帮着做科学计算，而且比 CPU 快得多。这招很别扭：得懂图形编程，还得把每个问题硬塞进画画的框框里（Buck 等 2004）。2006 年 11 月，NVIDIA 推出 GeForce 8800 显卡时，同时推出了 CUDA：一套让人用接近 C 语言的方式，直接给 GPU 写通用程序的东西（NVIDIA 2006），2007 年 6 月发布 1.0 版（NVIDIA 2007）。By the early 2000s, graphics cards could already run programs that computed the colour of each pixel. Some researchers found that if you disguised a large array as an image and a computation as "colouring in the pixels", the graphics card could help with scientific computing, and much faster than a CPU. The trick was awkward: you had to know graphics programming and squeeze every problem into the mould of drawing pictures (Buck et al. 2004). In November 2006, when NVIDIA launched the GeForce 8800 graphics card, it launched CUDA alongside it: a way to write general-purpose programs directly for the GPU in something close to the C language (NVIDIA 2006). Version 1.0 came out in June 2007 (NVIDIA 2007).

CUDA 这个词，指的其实是好几样东西叠在一起：The word CUDA actually covers several things stacked on top of one another:

  • 一种写法（编程模型）：你只写"一个线程做什么"的一个函数，叫核函数（kernel）；启动时说要多少个线程，它们被分成一个个线程块，整个排成一张网格。每个线程算出自己的编号，去处理属于自己的那一份数据。同一个块里的线程能共用一小块很快的片上存储、互相等一等；GPU 实际上以 32 个线程为一组（叫一个 warp）同步地执行同一条指令。A way of writing (the programming model): you write just one function, saying "what one thread does", called a kernel; when you launch it you say how many threads you want, and they are divided into thread blocks, which together are laid out as a grid. Each thread works out its own index and goes off to handle its own share of the data. Threads in the same block can share a small piece of very fast on-chip memory and wait for one another; in fact the GPU runs threads in groups of 32 (each called a warp) that execute the same instruction in lockstep.
  • 一套工具：编译器 nvcc 把程序翻译成一种"虚拟指令"（PTX）和当时几代 GPU 各自的机器指令，一起放进程序里；碰上更新的 GPU，驱动在运行时再把 PTX 翻译成它的机器指令，所以多年前写的程序在新 GPU 上还能跑；还有运行库、驱动、调试和性能分析工具。A set of tools: the compiler, nvcc, translates the program into "virtual instructions" (PTX) plus the machine instructions of each GPU generation around at the time, and packs them into the program together; when the program meets a newer GPU, the driver translates the PTX into that GPU’s machine instructions at run time, which is why programs written years ago still run on new GPUs. Then there are the runtime library, the driver, and tools for debugging and profiling.
  • 一大堆现成的库：矩阵乘法（cuBLAS）、神经网络的各种层（cuDNN）、多块 GPU 之间交换数据（NCCL）、把训练好的模型优化成推理用的程序（TensorRT）……PyTorch 这些框架在 NVIDIA 的 GPU 上跑，靠的就是它们。A big pile of ready-made libraries: matrix multiplication (cuBLAS), the various layers of neural networks (cuDNN), exchanging data between GPUs (NCCL), turning a trained model into an optimised program for inference (TensorRT)… Frameworks such as PyTorch rely on these to run on NVIDIA GPUs.
i = blockIdx.x × blockDim.x + threadIdx.xy[i] = a · x[i] + y[i]

每个线程用"我在第几个块、每块多少个线程、我是块里的第几个"算出自己负责第 i 个元素，然后只算这一个元素：y 的第 i 个数，等于 a 乘 x 的第 i 个数，再加上原来的 y。Each thread uses "which block I am in, how many threads each block has, and which thread I am within my block" to work out that it is responsible for element i, and then computes just that one element: the i-th number of y becomes a times the i-th number of x, plus its old value.

这是 CUDA 里最常举的例子（叫 SAXPY）。写程序的人不写循环，只写循环体；"循环"变成了成千上万个线程，同时各做一圈。GPU 把线程块分给几十到一百多个流式多处理器（SM，可以理解成 GPU 里的"大核"），每个 SM 同时养着几十个 warp：哪个 warp 在等内存，就先跑另一个，用"一直有活干"来掩盖内存的延迟。这种写法让同一份程序自动用满大大小小的 GPU：SM 多的 GPU，一次多发几个块而已。This is the example CUDA is most often explained with (it is called SAXPY). The programmer writes no loop, only the loop body; the "loop" becomes thousands upon thousands of threads, each doing one pass at the same time. The GPU deals the thread blocks out to anything from a few dozen to over a hundred streaming multiprocessors (SMs, which you can think of as the GPU’s "big cores"), and each SM keeps dozens of warps going at once: when one warp is waiting for memory, it runs another, hiding the memory latency by always having work to do. Written this way, the same program automatically fills GPUs large and small: a GPU with more SMs simply sends out a few more blocks at a time.

i
这个线程负责的元素编号the index of the element this thread is responsible for
blockIdx.x
线程块在网格里的编号（从 0 开始）the index of the thread block within the grid (starting from 0)
blockDim.x
每个线程块有多少个线程（常用 128、256）the number of threads in each thread block (128 or 256 is common)
threadIdx.x
线程在自己块里的编号the thread’s index within its own block
a, x, y
一个数和两个长度相同的数组a number and two arrays of the same length

x 和 y 各有 100 万个数，每块 256 个线程：要 ⌈106 / 256⌉ = 3907 个块，每块 8 个 warp。第 3 个块（blockIdx.x = 2）里的第 5 个线程（threadIdx.x = 4）负责 i = 2 × 256 + 4 = 516。Say x and y hold 1 million numbers each, with 256 threads per block: that takes ⌈106 / 256⌉ = 3907 blocks, each of 8 warps. The 5th thread (threadIdx.x = 4) in the 3rd block (blockIdx.x = 2) handles i = 2 × 256 + 4 = 516.

warp 里的 32 个线程走的是同一条指令。要是程序里有 if，一半线程走这边、一半走那边，GPU 只能先让一半跑、另一半等，再反过来，速度减半。所以 GPU 喜欢"人人都做一样的事"，矩阵乘法正合适，到处分支的程序就不合适。The 32 threads in a warp all follow the same instruction. If the program has an if, and half the threads go one way and half the other, the GPU has to let one half run while the other waits, and then the other way round, so the speed halves. So GPUs like "everyone doing the same thing": matrix multiplication suits them perfectly; programs that branch everywhere do not.

为什么今天大多数人选 NVIDIAWhy most people choose NVIDIA today

2012 年，多伦多大学的三个人用两块 NVIDIA 的游戏显卡（GTX 580，每块 3 GB 显存），花五六天训练出一个卷积神经网络，在 ImageNet 图像识别比赛上大幅领先，这就是 AlexNet（Krizhevsky 等 2012）。从那以后，深度学习大多长在 NVIDIA 的 GPU 和 CUDA 上。它能一直领先，靠的不是某一块芯片，而是叠在一起的几层：In 2012 three people at the University of Toronto used two NVIDIA gaming cards (GTX 580s, with 3 GB of memory each) to train a convolutional neural network over five or six days, and it finished far ahead of the field in the ImageNet image-recognition competition: this was AlexNet (Krizhevsky et al. 2012). Since then, deep learning has mostly grown up on NVIDIA GPUs and CUDA. What has kept NVIDIA ahead is not any one chip but several layers stacked together:

  • 软件：CUDA 已经做了快二十年，每一代新 GPU 出来，NVIDIA 自己的矩阵乘法、通信这些库很快就为它调好，社区写的注意力核函数也多半先为它写；大多数论文的代码、开源模型，首先在 CUDA 上能跑。NVIDIA 2026 年初的年报说，用 CUDA 的开发者超过 750 万（NVIDIA 2026）；2008 年时只有几万（Nickolls 等 2008）。新的硬件功能（比如 FP8、FP4）也总是先在 CUDA 里能用。Software: CUDA has been around for nearly twenty years. Whenever a new GPU generation comes out, NVIDIA’s own libraries for matrix multiplication, communication and the like are quickly tuned for it, and the attention kernels the community writes mostly target it first; the code for most papers, and most open models, runs on CUDA first. NVIDIA’s annual report of early 2026 says more than 7.5 million developers use CUDA (NVIDIA 2026); in 2008 there were only tens of thousands (Nickolls et al. 2008). New hardware features (such as FP8 and FP4) also always become usable in CUDA first.
  • 整台机器：NVIDIA 卖的不只是芯片，还有把 GPU 连在一起的 NVLink 和交换芯片，2019 年宣布、2020 年完成收购的 Mellanox 带来了 InfiniBand 网络（NVIDIA 2020），再到一整柜 72 块 GPU 当一台机器用的 NVL72（第 ⑨ 步）。The whole machine: NVIDIA sells not only chips but also NVLink and the switch chips that join GPUs together; Mellanox, whose purchase was announced in 2019 and completed in 2020, brought InfiniBand networking (NVIDIA 2020); and it goes all the way up to NVL72, a whole rack of 72 GPUs used as one machine (step ⑨).
  • 节奏和产能：差不多每年出一代新产品（新架构约两年一代，中间一年是同一架构的加强版）；台积电的先进封装产能和 HBM 早早订下。Pace and capacity: a new generation of products almost every year (a new architecture about every two years, with an upgraded version of the same architecture in the year between); TSMC’s advanced-packaging capacity and HBM booked well in advance.

结果是：IoT Analytics 估计，2024 年数据中心 GPU 市场里 NVIDIA 占 92%，AMD 占 4%（IoT Analytics 2025）；NVIDIA 最近一个季度（2026 年 5 到 7 月）收入 962 亿美元，其中 890 亿来自数据中心（NVIDIA 2026）。不过只看"GPU 市场"会夸大它：要是把各家自己设计的专用芯片也算上，TrendForce 预计 2026 年出货的 AI 服务器里，用 GPU 的约占 70%，用 Google 的 TPU、亚马逊的 Trainium 这类专用芯片的约占 28%（TrendForce 2026）。机器人这边也类似：主计算模块多用 NVIDIA 的 Jetson，它也跑 CUDA，数据中心训练好的模型可以几乎原样搬上去；但高通 2026 年初也推出了面向人形机器人的 Dragonwing IQ10，Figure 在和它一起定义下一代计算平台（Qualcomm 2026）。The result: IoT Analytics estimates that in 2024 NVIDIA had 92% of the data-centre GPU market and AMD 4% (IoT Analytics 2025); in its latest quarter (May to July 2026) NVIDIA’s revenue was $96.2 billion, $89 billion of it from data centres (NVIDIA 2026). But looking only at the "GPU market" overstates its position: if the accelerators that companies design for themselves are counted too, TrendForce expects that of the AI servers shipped in 2026, about 70% will use GPUs and about 28% accelerators such as Google’s TPU and Amazon’s Trainium (TrendForce 2026). On the robot side it is similar: main compute modules are mostly NVIDIA’s Jetson, which also runs CUDA, so models trained in the data centre can move onto it almost unchanged; but in early 2026 Qualcomm also launched the Dragonwing IQ10 for humanoid robots, and Figure is working with Qualcomm to define a next-generation computing platform (Qualcomm 2026).

它的代价Its costs

领先不等于每件事都做得最好。GPU 是一种通用的并行芯片：它要照顾图形、科学计算和各种各样的神经网络，所以带着不少某一件具体的事用不上的部件。只做一件事的专用芯片可以把面积和电都花在那一件事上：Google 2017 年发表的测量里，只做神经网络推理的第一代 TPU，每瓦的运算次数是同时代 GPU 和 CPU 的 30 到 80 倍（Jouppi 等 2017）；不过比的是 2014 年、还没有张量核心的 K80，NVIDIA 从 2017 年起也给 GPU 加上了专做矩阵乘法的张量核心。其次，GPU 也躲不开内存墙：逐词生成时，它那几 PFLOPS 的算力大多在等 HBM（第 ③、⑦ 步）。再次，它耗电、也贵：一块 B200 最多 1000 W；Epoch AI 估算，一个 1 GW 的 AI 数据中心每年约 85 亿美元的总成本里，服务器约占六成（Epoch AI 2026）。还有被一家锁住的风险：代码写在 CUDA 上，换芯片就要重写、重调；NVIDIA 的许可协议还禁止把用 CUDA 工具编译出来的程序翻译到别家的芯片上跑（NVIDIA 2026）。最后是供应和政治：先进封装和 HBM 的产能有限；美国对华出口管制时紧时松，中国又让企业停订 NVIDIA 的芯片、推数据中心改用国产（Tom’s Hardware 2026），NVIDIA 2026 年 8 月的业绩指引已经不计入任何来自中国的数据中心算力收入（NVIDIA 2026）。Leading is not the same as doing everything best. A GPU is a general-purpose parallel chip: it has to look after graphics, scientific computing and every kind of neural network, so it carries quite a few parts that any one particular job does not use. An accelerator that does only one thing can spend all its area and power on that one thing: in measurements Google published in 2017, the first TPU, which did only neural-network inference, delivered 30 to 80 times as many operations per watt as the GPUs and CPUs of its day (Jouppi et al. 2017); though the GPU it was compared with was the K80 of 2014, which had no tensor cores, and NVIDIA has been adding tensor cores built for matrix multiplication to its GPUs since 2017. Second, GPUs cannot escape the memory wall either: during decode (token-by-token generation), most of their several PFLOPS of compute sits waiting for HBM (steps ③ and ⑦). Third, they are power-hungry and expensive: one B200 draws up to 1000 W; Epoch AI estimates that servers make up about 60% of the roughly $8.5 billion a year that a 1 GW AI data centre costs in total (Epoch AI 2026). Then there is the risk of being locked in to one company: code written for CUDA has to be rewritten and re-tuned to change chips, and NVIDIA’s licence agreement also forbids translating programs compiled with CUDA tools to run on other companies’ chips (NVIDIA 2026). Finally, supply and politics: advanced-packaging and HBM capacity is limited; US export controls on China tighten and loosen by turns, while China has told companies to stop ordering NVIDIA chips and is pushing data centres to switch to domestic ones (Tom’s Hardware 2026), and NVIDIA’s guidance of August 2026 already counts no data-centre compute revenue from China at all (NVIDIA 2026).

已经在跑的别的路Other routes already in use

正因为有这些代价，别的路一直有人在走，下面几条已经是规模不小的产品。它们的难处大多相同：芯片未必比 GPU 慢，难的是让建在 CUDA 上的代码和手工调到极致的核函数，在新芯片上也一样快、一样稳。Because of these costs, people have kept working on other routes, and the ones below are already sizeable products. They mostly share the same difficulty: the chip is not necessarily slower than a GPU; the hard part is getting code built on CUDA, and kernels hand-tuned to the limit, to run just as fast and just as reliably on the new chip.

路线Route谁在做Who长处，解决什么Strengths, what it solves卡在哪What holds it back
另一家的 GPUAnother company’s GPUsAMD 的 Instinct GPU 和 ROCm 软件。OpenAI 2025 年 10 月和 AMD 签下 6 GW 的 GPU（AMD 2025）AMD’s Instinct GPUs and ROCm software. In October 2025 OpenAI signed with AMD for 6 GW of GPUs (AMD 2025)单卡显存更大：MI450 有 432 GB HBM4、19.6 TB/s（Tom’s Hardware 2025），大模型要的 GPU 更少。ROCm 里的 HIP 几乎照搬 CUDA 的写法，还有工具（HIPIFY）把 CUDA 源代码自动改写过去（AMD）More memory per GPU: the MI450 has 432 GB of HBM4 at 19.6 TB/s (Tom’s Hardware 2025), so a large model needs fewer GPUs. HIP in ROCm copies CUDA’s programming model almost exactly, and a tool (HIPIFY) rewrites CUDA source code for it automatically (AMD)库和工具没那么全，最新的手调核函数常常晚一步：FlashAttention 的最新版本先为 NVIDIA 的 Hopper、Blackwell 写，AMD 用的还是早一代的做法（FlashAttention）Libraries and tools are less complete, and the newest hand-tuned kernels often come a step later: the latest versions of FlashAttention are written first for NVIDIA’s Hopper and Blackwell, while AMD still uses the previous generation’s approach (FlashAttention)
专用芯片（脉动阵列）Accelerators (systolic arrays)Google 的 TPU，配 XLA 编译器和 JAX（JAX）；亚马逊的 Trainium，配 Neuron。Anthropic 同时用 TPU、Trainium 和 NVIDIA 的 GPU（Anthropic 2025）Google’s TPU, with the XLA compiler and JAX (JAX); Amazon’s Trainium, with Neuron. Anthropic uses TPUs, Trainium and NVIDIA GPUs side by side (Anthropic 2025)只做矩阵乘法和少数几件事，面积和电花在刀刃上（第 ⑤ 步）。第 7 代 TPU（Ironwood）每块 FP8 4614 TFLOPS、192 GiB（约 206 GB）HBM，一个 pod 连 9216 块（Google Cloud）They do only matrix multiplication and a few other things, so the area and the power go where they count (step ⑤). The 7th-generation TPU (Ironwood) has 4614 TFLOPS of FP8 and 192 GiB (about 206 GB) of HBM per chip, and one pod links 9216 chips (Google Cloud)基本只能在自家的云里租；软件是另一套，从 CUDA 迁过去要改代码；模型结构要是大变，固定的硬件未必跟得上Mostly available only to rent in the maker’s own cloud; the software is a separate stack, so moving over from CUDA means changing code; if model architectures change a lot, fixed hardware may not keep up
