A whole wafer is bound to have defects, so about 7% of the cores are kept as spares to route around them (only 900,000 of 970,000 cores are enabled, Cerebras 2025); the cost, power delivery and cooling of a whole wafer are all hard too
只用 SRAM 的推理芯片SRAM-only inference chipsGroq（LPU）。2025 年 12 月，它把推理技术非独家授权给 NVIDIA，创始人等加入 NVIDIA，Groq 继续独立经营（Constellation Research 2025）Groq (LPU). In December 2025 it licensed its inference technology to NVIDIA non-exclusively; its founder and others joined NVIDIA, and Groq carries on as an independent company (Constellation Research 2025)权重常驻在每块芯片几百 MB 的 SRAM 里，不等 HBM，每个词的延迟低而且稳定The weights stay resident in each chip’s few hundred MB of SRAM, with no waiting for HBM, so the latency per token is low and steady一块芯片才几百 MB，一个 70 GB 的模型要上百块芯片：适合求快，不省钱A chip holds only a few hundred MB, so a 70 GB model needs over a hundred chips: good for speed, not for saving money
国产芯片Chinese chips华为昇腾，配 CANN 软件；Atlas 950 超节点最多连 8192 块 NPU（华为 2025）Huawei Ascend, with CANN software; an Atlas 950 SuperPoD links up to 8192 NPUs (Huawei 2025)出口管制下中国的数据中心买得到。IDC 的数据：2025 年中国约 400 万块 AI 加速卡里，国内厂商约占 41%（Reuters 2026）Data centres in China can buy them under export controls. IDC figures: of about 4 million AI accelerator cards in China in 2025, Chinese makers supplied about 41% (Reuters 2026)拿不到最先进的工艺，HBM 要自己做；华为 2026 年 9 月说产能满足不了国内需求（Tom’s Hardware 2026）；CANN 的生态还在建No access to the most advanced manufacturing processes, and it has to make its own HBM; in September 2026 Huawei said its capacity could not meet domestic demand (Tom’s Hardware 2026); the CANN ecosystem is still being built

还有一条路是往上走一层，不去替换芯片，而是让代码不再绑在一家芯片上：PyTorch 2 的编译器自动生成用 Triton 写的核函数，而 Triton 能编译到 NVIDIA 和 AMD 的 GPU 上（Triton）；JAX 写的程序经 XLA 可以跑在 TPU 和 GPU 上。换芯片时要改的代码越来越少，但最快的那几个核函数，今天仍然多半是先在 CUDA 上手工写出来的。Another route goes one level up: instead of replacing the chip, it unties the code from any one company’s chips. The PyTorch 2 compiler automatically generates kernels written in Triton, and Triton compiles to both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs (Triton); programs written in JAX run on TPUs and GPUs through XLA. Less and less code has to change when you switch chips, but today the very fastest kernels are still mostly written by hand in CUDA first.

这些都是今天买得到、租得到的产品，本质上还是"把数从存储搬到运算单元再算"。更远一些，还有几条路线想换掉这个做法：把计算放进存储里、用光来算或者用光来传、学大脑只在有事时才动……它们分别冲着前面哪个问题去、哪些学校和公司在推进、为什么今天还没落地，第 ⑮ 步一条一条地讲。These are all products you can buy or rent today, and at heart they still "move the numbers from memory to the arithmetic units, then compute". Further out, several routes aim to replace that approach: putting the computing inside the memory, computing with light or carrying data with light, acting only when something happens, as the brain does… Step ⑮ goes through them one by one: which of the problems above each one targets, which universities and companies are pushing it, and why it has not reached commercial use yet.

  • 第一块是 CUDA 的写法：拖元素个数 N、选每块线程数，看要多少个块、多少个 warp；点一个格子，看这个线程的 blockIdx、threadIdx 和它算出的 i。第二块是一块 GPU（B200，148 个 SM）：线程块被一批批分给各个 SM。The first panel is the CUDA model: drag Elements N and choose Threads per block to see how many blocks and how many warps it takes; tap a cell to see that thread’s blockIdx and threadIdx and the i it works out. The second panel is one GPU (a B200, 148 SMs): the thread blocks are dealt out to the SMs in waves.
  • 第三块是分支：让一个 warp 里一半线程走 if、一半走 else，看它慢了多少。The third panel is Branches: let half the threads in a warp take the if and half the else, and see how much slower it gets.
  • 最后一块是 CUDA 由哪几层组成，旁边是其他厂家对应的东西。点一项，下面写出它是什么、谁在做；别家的几项和 Triton 还写出长处和短板。The last panel shows the layers CUDA is made of, with the other vendors’ equivalents beside them. Tap an item and the text below says what it is and who makes it; for the other vendors’ items and for Triton it also gives strengths and weaknesses.

先玩：N = 100 万、每块 256 个线程：要多少个块？这块 GPU 要分几批才发完？点"一半走 if"：这个 warp 的效率还剩多少？最后点一点下面那几层：PyTorch 在哪一层？Try first: N = 1,000,000 and 256 threads per block: how many blocks? In how many waves does this GPU deal them all out? Press "Half if, half else": how much of the warp’s efficiency is left? Finally tap through the layers at the bottom: which layer is PyTorch in?

这一步的要点：CUDA 是一种写法（写一个线程做什么，启动成千上万个）、一套把它编译成 GPU 指令的工具、和一大堆调好的库。NVIDIA 的领先靠的是近二十年的软件、把 GPU 连成整台机器的网络和产能；代价是通用芯片不是每件事都最省、耗电、贵、被一家锁住。AMD 的 GPU、Google 和亚马逊的专用芯片、Cerebras、Groq、华为昇腾都已经是产品，各有长处，难处多半在软件生态。The point of this step: CUDA is a programming model (write what one thread does, then launch thousands of them), a set of tools that compiles it into GPU instructions, and a big collection of tuned libraries. NVIDIA’s lead rests on nearly twenty years of software, the networking that joins GPUs into whole machines, and production capacity; the price is that a general-purpose chip is not the most efficient at everything, and that it is power-hungry, expensive and locks you in to one company. AMD’s GPUs, Google’s and Amazon’s accelerators, Cerebras, Groq and Huawei Ascend are all products already, each with its strengths; their difficulties lie mostly in the software ecosystem.

第 ⑦ 步 · 大模型的一次计算Step ⑦ · One pass through a large model

一个词要算多少次、读多少字节How many operations and bytes one token takes

先把大模型拆开看一眼（第 4 篇讲过 Transformer 的细节）。一句话先被切成词元（token）：常见的词是一个词元，生僻的拆成几块，一个汉字大约是一到两个词元。每个词元变成一串 d 个数的向量。这串向量依次穿过 L 层，每一层做两件事：注意力，让它回头看看前面所有的词元，从中取需要的信息；前馈网络，对它自己做一次变换。两件事几乎全是矩阵乘法。穿过最后一层，向量变成对词表里每个词元的打分，挑一个出来，就是下一个词元。然后把这个新词元接到后面，再来一遍。First, a quick look inside a large model (page 4 covered the Transformer in detail). A sentence is first cut into tokens: a common word is one token, a rare one is split into several pieces, and a Chinese character is roughly one or two tokens. Each token becomes a vector of d numbers. This vector passes through L layers in turn, and every layer does two things: attention, which lets it look back at all the earlier tokens and take the information it needs from them, and a feed-forward network, which transforms it on its own. Both are almost entirely matrix multiplication. After the last layer the vector becomes a score for every token in the vocabulary; pick one, and that is the next token. Then the new token is appended and the whole thing runs again.

Nop ≈ 2N, S = N · bMKV = 2 · L · hkv · dh · b · T

生成一个词元，大约要做"参数个数的两倍"次运算，要读一遍全部参数，也就是 N 乘每个参数的字节数。另外，前面每个词元在每一层留下的"键"和"值"要存起来，一共占 2 乘层数、乘键值头数、乘每个头的维数、乘每个数的字节数、再乘词元个数这么多字节。Generating one token takes about "twice the number of parameters" operations and one read of all the parameters, that is, N times the bytes per parameter. On top of that, the "keys" and "values" that each earlier token left in each layer must be stored; they take 2 times the number of layers, times the number of key-value heads, times the dimension of each head, times the bytes per number, times the number of tokens, in bytes.

第一行：每个权重在这个词元上恰好用一次，做一次乘加，也就是两次运算；而它必须先从显存搬到运算单元跟前。第二行：注意力要拿当前词元去和前面每一个词元比较，用到它们在每一层算出的两个向量，叫键（K）和值（V）。每次都重算太浪费，所以算过就存起来，叫键值缓存（KV cache）。上下文越长，它越大，而且每生成一个词元都要整个读一遍。现在的模型让好几个注意力头共用一组键值（分组查询注意力），hkv 比注意力头数少好几倍，就是为了让这块缓存小一点。First line: each weight is used exactly once for this token, in one multiply–accumulate, which is two operations; and it must first be moved from GPU memory up to the arithmetic units. Second line: attention compares the current token with every earlier token, using two vectors each earlier token produced in every layer, called the key (K) and the value (V). Recomputing them every time would be wasteful, so once computed they are kept: this is the KV cache. The longer the context, the bigger it gets, and it must be read in full for every token generated. Today’s models let several attention heads share one set of keys and values (grouped-query attention), so hkv is several times smaller than the number of attention heads: the point is to make this cache smaller.

N
模型的参数个数（"8B"就是 80 亿）the number of parameters in the model ("8B" means 8 billion)
Nop
生成一个词元要做的运算次数（第 ④ 步的 FLOP）operations to generate one token (the FLOP of step ④)
b
每个数占几字节：BF16 是 2，FP8 是 1bytes per number: 2 for BF16, 1 for FP8
S
全部参数占的字节数bytes taken by all the parameters
L
层数number of layers
hkv, dh
每层有几组键值头；每个头的向量有几个数key-value heads per layer; numbers in each head’s vector
T
上下文里已经有几个词元tokens already in the context
MKV
键值缓存占的字节数bytes taken by the KV cache

规划模型按开源的 Llama 3.1 8B 的结构：L = 32 层，hkv = 8，dh = 128（Grattafiori 等 2024）。生成一个词元约 1.6 × 1010 次运算；用 BF16 存时参数 16 GB，键值缓存每个词元 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131 kB。上下文到 128 000 个词元时，键值缓存是 16.8 GB，比模型本身还大。机器人的三台相机要是每秒看 10 次、每张图 256 个词元，一分钟就是 46 万个词元，键值缓存 60 GB（第 ⑪ 步）。The planner follows the structure of the open-source Llama 3.1 8B: L = 32 layers, hkv = 8, dh = 128 (Grattafiori et al. 2024). One token takes about 1.6 × 1010 operations; stored in BF16 the parameters take 16 GB, and the KV cache takes 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131 kB per token. At 128,000 tokens of context the KV cache is 16.8 GB, bigger than the model itself. If the model looks at the robot’s three cameras 10 times a second, at 256 tokens an image, one minute comes to 460,000 tokens and the KV cache to 60 GB (step ⑪).

所以"更大的显存"要装的不只是模型，还有每个用户、每段对话的键值缓存；上下文越长、同时用的人越多，它越大。So "more GPU memory" has to hold not only the model but also the KV cache of every user and every conversation; the longer the context and the more people using it at once, the bigger that gets.

预填充和逐词生成Prefill and decode

模型回答一个问题分两段。先是预填充：把你的问题（比如几百个词元）一次全部送进去，所有词元一起穿过每一层，把它们的键值存进缓存。这时每个权重一搬到跟前，就和几百个词元的向量各乘一次：搬一次，用几百次。然后是逐词生成：一次只生成一个词元，每个权重搬来只用一次，用完就扔，下一个词元再搬。两段的性质完全不同：前一段卡在算力上，后一段卡在内存带宽上。A model answers a question in two phases. First comes prefill: your whole question (a few hundred tokens, say) goes in at once, all the tokens pass through every layer together, and their keys and values are stored in the cache. Each weight, once it has been moved up to the arithmetic units, is multiplied with the vectors of all those hundreds of tokens: moved once, used hundreds of times. Then comes decode: just one token is generated at a time, so each weight moved in is used only once, then thrown away, and moved in again for the next token. The two phases are completely different in character: the first is limited by compute, the second by memory bandwidth.

I = Nop / NBP = min(Ppeak, I · BW), I* = Ppeak / BW

一段计算里，每搬一个字节能做几次运算，叫它的算术强度 I。芯片实际能跑出的算力，是"峰值算力"和"算术强度乘带宽"两者中较小的那个。两者相等的那个强度 I*，叫拐点。The number of operations a computation does for each byte it moves is its arithmetic intensity I. The compute a chip actually achieves is the smaller of "peak compute" and "arithmetic intensity times bandwidth". The intensity I* at which the two are equal is called the ridge point.

把横轴画成算术强度、纵轴画成实际算力（都用对数刻度），这条"先斜着上升、再变平"的折线叫屋顶线（Williams 等 2009）。强度低于拐点，运算单元在等数据，是内存受限；高于拐点，数据管够，是算力受限。逐词生成时，一个人用：每个参数（b 字节）做 2 次运算，I = 2 / b，FP8 时只有 2；一批 B 个人同时生成，一份参数给 B 个人用，I ≈ 2B / b；预填充 T 个词元，I ≈ 2T / b。Put arithmetic intensity on the horizontal axis and achieved compute on the vertical (both on log scales), and this line that "first climbs at a slant, then goes flat" is called the roofline (Williams et al. 2009). Below the ridge point the arithmetic units wait for data: the computation is memory-bound. Above it the data keep up: it is compute-bound. In decode for one user, each parameter (b bytes) does 2 operations, so I = 2 / b, only 2 in FP8; when a batch of B users generate at once, one copy of the parameters serves all B, so I ≈ 2B / b; for a prefill of T tokens, I ≈ 2T / b.

I
算术强度，FLOP/字节arithmetic intensity, FLOP/byte
NB
这段计算从显存（内存）搬的字节数bytes this computation moves from GPU memory (or RAM)
Ppeak
芯片在这种精度下的峰值算力，FLOPSthe chip’s peak compute at this precision, FLOPS
BW
显存（内存）带宽，字节/秒GPU memory (or RAM) bandwidth, bytes/s
P
实际能跑出的算力compute actually achieved
I*
拐点ridge point

一块 B200 用 FP8：稠密峰值约 4.5 PFLOPS（NVIDIA），带宽约 8 TB/s，拐点 I* = 4.5 × 1015 / (8 × 1012) ≈ 560。一个人用 8B 模型逐词生成，I = 2：只能跑出 2 × 8 TB/s = 16 TFLOPS，峰值的 0.4%；要把运算单元喂饱，得凑大约 280 个人一起生成。机器人上的 Jetson Thor 只公布了 FP4 稀疏的峰值 2070 TFLOPS（NVIDIA 2026）；用 FP4 逐词生成时每个参数 0.5 字节，I = 2 / 0.5 = 4，带宽 273 GB/s 只够跑出 4 × 273 GB/s ≈ 1.1 TFLOPS，是那个标称值的 0.05%。One B200 in FP8: a dense peak of about 4.5 PFLOPS (NVIDIA), bandwidth about 8 TB/s, ridge point I* = 4.5 × 1015 / (8 × 1012) ≈ 560. One user decoding the 8B model has I = 2: it reaches only 2 × 8 TB/s = 16 TFLOPS, 0.4% of the peak; to keep the arithmetic units fed you would have to batch about 280 users generating together. For the Jetson Thor on the robot, the only published peak is for sparse FP4, 2070 TFLOPS (NVIDIA 2026); decoding in FP4, each parameter is 0.5 bytes, so I = 2 / 0.5 = 4, and the 273 GB/s of bandwidth is enough for only 4 × 273 GB/s ≈ 1.1 TFLOPS, 0.05% of that headline figure.

这就是数据中心为什么拼命把请求凑成批：一个人用的时候，99% 的运算单元在等内存。机器人只有它自己一个"用户"，凑不成批，所以它几乎永远在拐点左边，内存带宽比算力更要紧（第 ⑫ 步）。That is why data centres try so hard to batch requests: with one user, 99% of the arithmetic units are waiting for memory. A robot has only one "user", itself, so it cannot batch; it sits almost always to the left of the ridge point, and memory bandwidth matters more than compute (step ⑫).

  • 屋顶线：横轴是算术强度，纵轴是实际算力，都是对数刻度。按钮选芯片，画出它的屋顶和拐点。The roofline: arithmetic intensity across, achieved compute up, both on log scales. The buttons pick a chip and draw its roof and ridge point.
  • 点是几种计算：逐词生成（一个人）、逐词生成（一批）、预填充、机器人的动作模型算一次。拖批大小和预填充的词元数，看点怎么移动；选模型和精度。The dots are different kinds of computation: decode (one user), decode (a batch), prefill, and one call of the robot’s action model. Drag Batch size and Prefill tokens to see how the dots move; pick a model and a precision.
  • 下面写着现在这个点的强度、实际算力、卡在哪，一个词元要多久，每秒能出几个词元。Below, it shows the current dot’s intensity, achieved compute and what limits it, how long one token takes and how many tokens come out per second.

先玩：选 B200、8B、FP8：一个人逐词生成时，运算单元用了百分之几？把批大小拖到多少，点才走到拐点？换成机器人的模块：拐点在哪？动作模型算一次，落在拐点的哪一边？Try first: pick B200, 8B and FP8: when one user decodes, what percentage of the arithmetic units is in use? How far must you drag the batch size for the dot to reach the ridge point? Switch to the robot’s module: where is its ridge point? Which side of it does one call of the action model land on?

这一步的要点：生成一个词元，约做 2N 次运算、读一遍全部参数，还要读整个键值缓存。预填充时一份参数用很多次，卡在算力上；逐词生成时一份参数只用一次，卡在内存带宽上。凑批能把强度抬上去，可机器人凑不成批。The point of this step: generating one token takes about 2N operations and one read of all the parameters, plus a read of the whole KV cache. In prefill each parameter is used many times, so it is limited by compute; in decode each parameter is used only once, so it is limited by memory bandwidth. Batching raises the intensity, but a robot cannot batch.

第 ⑧ 步 · 一个词走一圈Step ⑧ · One token’s round trip

从一个问题到一个词：它在硬件里经过了哪些地方From a question to a word: where it travels in the hardware

假设台面上有两杯水，机器人拿不准你要哪一杯。它身上的规划模型不够聪明，就把头部相机的照片和你那句话发给数据中心里一个大得多的模型（比如 700 亿参数），问："他说的是哪一杯？"模型一个词元一个词元地回答："左边那杯"。我们跟着其中一个词元，看它在硬件里走过的路。Suppose there are two glasses of water on the counter and the robot can’t tell which one you want. Its on-board planning model isn’t clever enough, so it sends the head camera’s photo and your sentence to a much larger model in a data centre (say, 70 billion parameters) and asks: "Which glass does he mean?" The model answers one token at a time: "The one on the left." We follow one of those tokens along its path through the hardware.

  • ① 出门
    照片和问题从机器人的 Wi-Fi 出去，经过路由器、运营商的网络，到达数据中心门口的服务器。这一段按距离和网络情况，要几毫秒到上百毫秒（第 ⑫ 步）。    ① Out
    The photo and the question leave over the robot’s Wi-Fi, pass through the router and the provider’s network, and reach a server at the data centre’s front door. Depending on the distance and the state of the network, this leg takes anywhere from a few milliseconds to over a hundred (step ⑫).
  • ② CPU 排队
    一台普通服务器的 CPU 收下请求，把文字切成词元、把图片切成小块，交给调度程序。调度程序把它和别的用户的请求凑成一批，分给一组 GPU：比如一台机器里用 NVLink 连在一起的 8 块 GPU。模型的参数早就分成 8 份，分别住在这 8 块 GPU 的显存里，不需要再搬。    ② Queueing at the CPU
    The CPU of an ordinary server takes in the request, cuts the text into tokens and the image into small patches, and hands them to the scheduler. The scheduler batches the request with other users’ requests and assigns the batch to a group of GPUs: for example, the 8 GPUs in one machine, linked together by NVLink. The model’s parameters were split into 8 parts long ago, each living in the memory of one of these 8 GPUs, so they don’t need to be moved.
  • ③ 预填充
    照片和问题的几百到几千个词元一起穿过 80 层，每层的键和值存进各 GPU 显存里的键值缓存。这一段是一份参数用很多次，卡在算力上（第 ⑦ 步）。    ③ Prefill
    The hundreds to thousands of tokens of the photo and the question pass through the 80 layers together, and each layer’s keys and values are stored in the KV cache in each GPU’s memory. In this stage each parameter, once read, is used many times, so the work is held back by compute (step ⑦).
  • ④ 逐词生成：一层一层
    生成一个词元时，每一层里：每块 GPU 把自己那一份权重从 HBM 搬进片上的缓存和寄存器，张量核心做矩阵乘法；注意力读出这个用户前面所有词元的键值；8 块 GPU 各算了一部分，要通过 NVLink 把部分结果加在一起（叫全规约，all-reduce），每层两次。然后进入下一层。    ④ Decode: layer by layer
    To generate one token, in each layer: every GPU moves its own share of the weights from HBM into the on-chip cache and registers, and the tensor cores do the matrix multiplications; attention reads the keys and values of all this user’s earlier tokens; each of the 8 GPUs has computed only part of the result, so the partial results must be added together over NVLink (this is called an all-reduce), twice per layer. Then on to the next layer.
  • ⑤ 出词
    最后一层的输出变成对词表里每个词元的打分，按概率挑一个。这个词元的编号（一个整数）交回 CPU，变回文字。    ⑤ Pick a token
    The last layer’s output becomes a score for every token in the vocabulary, and one is picked according to the probabilities. That token’s id (an integer) goes back to the CPU and is turned back into text.
  • ⑥ 回家
    文字顺着网络回到机器人。同时，这个新词元已经被接到输入后面，下一个词元开始走 ④。    ⑥ Home
    The text travels back over the network to the robot. Meanwhile the new token has already been appended to the input, and the next token sets off on ④.
ttok ≈ S / (G · BW) + MKV / (G · BW) + 2 L · tar + tother

一个词元在 GPU 里要花的时间，大约是：每块 GPU 读自己那份参数的时间，加上读自己那份键值缓存的时间，加上每层两次全规约的时间，再加上其他零碎的时间。The time one token spends in the GPUs is roughly: the time for each GPU to read its share of the parameters, plus the time to read its share of the KV cache, plus the time for two all-reduces per layer, plus other overheads.

逐词生成时运算单元大多在等数据（第 ⑦ 步），所以第一项是主角：模型切成 G 份，每块 GPU 只读 S/G 字节，G 块一起读，相当于带宽变成 G 倍。代价是第三项：每层都要停下来两次，等 8 块 GPU 交换部分结果，这一下的延迟很难再压，层数越多越显眼。这就是为什么切模型要切在 NVLink 连着的同一组 GPU 里：要是隔着普通网络，每层多等几十微秒，80 层下来就是好几毫秒。During decode the arithmetic units spend most of their time waiting for data (step ⑦), so the first term dominates: split the model into G parts and each GPU reads only S/G bytes; with G GPUs reading at once, it is as if the bandwidth were G times as large. The price is the third term: twice in every layer, everything has to stop and wait while the 8 GPUs exchange their partial results. That delay is hard to cut any further, and the more layers there are, the more it shows. That is why a model is split only within a group of GPUs linked by NVLink: over an ordinary network, each layer would wait tens of microseconds longer, which over 80 layers adds up to several milliseconds.

ttok
生成一个词元的时间（不算网络）time to generate one token (not counting the network)
S, MKV
参数的总字节数；这一批用户的键值缓存的总字节数total bytes of the parameters; total bytes of the KV cache for this batch of users
G
模型被切成几份、放在几块 GPU 上how many parts the model is cut into, and so how many GPUs it runs on
BW
每块 GPU 的显存带宽memory bandwidth of each GPU
L, tar
层数；一次全规约的时间（数据量很小，主要是延迟）number of layers; time for one all-reduce (very little data, so mostly latency)
tother
启动核函数、出词、调度这些零碎的时间other overheads: launching kernels, picking the token, scheduling

70B 模型用 FP8 存，S = 70 GB，切成 8 份放在 8 块 B200 上：每块读 8.75 GB，按 8 TB/s 约 1.1 ms。照片加问题约 2000 个词元，键值缓存（BF16）每个词元 328 kB（L = 80，hkv = 8，dh = 128，Grattafiori 等 2024），一共 0.66 GB，每块 82 MB，读一遍约 0.01 ms。80 层、每层两次全规约，一共 160 次；每次的数据很小，时间主要是延迟，这里假设每次 5 µs，合起来 0.8 ms。零碎的时间先不算，一个词元约 1.9 ms，一个用户每秒最多约 525 个词元。这是理想的上限：实际系统里带宽用不满、核函数要启动，还会慢一些；NVIDIA 测过一个张量并行的模型，逐词生成时光是全规约就占了约 23% 的时间（NVIDIA 2025）。一批 64 个用户同时生成时，读参数的 1.1 ms 由大家共用，每人的键值缓存却要各读各的：每块 GPU 读 64 × 82 MB ≈ 5.2 GB，约 0.66 ms，一步约 2.55 ms。每个人每秒约 390 个词元，慢了约四分之一，整组 GPU 每秒却能出约 25 000 个词元，是一个人用时的近 50 倍。A 70B model stored in FP8 has S = 70 GB; split 8 ways across 8 B200s, each GPU reads 8.75 GB, about 1.1 ms at 8 TB/s. The photo plus the question come to about 2000 tokens, and the KV cache (BF16) takes 328 kB per token (L = 80, hkv = 8, dh = 128, Grattafiori et al. 2024): 0.66 GB in all, 82 MB per GPU, about 0.01 ms to read. With 80 layers and two all-reduces per layer, there are 160 all-reduces; each carries very little data, so its time is mostly latency, and assuming 5 µs each they add up to 0.8 ms. Leaving the other overheads aside for now, one token takes about 1.9 ms, so one user gets at most about 525 tokens a second. That is the ideal upper limit: in a real system the bandwidth is never fully used and kernels have to be launched, so it is somewhat slower; NVIDIA measured a tensor-parallel model in which the all-reduces alone took about 23% of the decode time (NVIDIA 2025). When a batch of 64 users generate at the same time, the 1.1 ms spent reading the parameters is shared by all of them, but each user’s KV cache has to be read separately: each GPU reads 64 × 82 MB ≈ 5.2 GB, about 0.66 ms, so one step takes about 2.55 ms. Each person gets about 390 tokens a second, about a quarter slower, but the group of GPUs as a whole turns out about 25,000 tokens a second, nearly 50 times as many as with one user.

对机器人来说，GPU 里这几毫秒往往不是大头，网络来回才是：几十到上百毫秒，还可能忽长忽短。所以要紧的、每秒要算很多次的事，必须在身上算；只有"偶尔问一个难题"才适合交给云端。For the robot, these few milliseconds in the GPUs are usually not the main cost; the network round trip is: tens to hundreds of milliseconds, and it can jump around. So whatever is urgent and has to be computed many times a second must be computed on board; only "asking a hard question now and then" is right for the cloud.

  • 预设：在机器人上用 8B、一块 B200 上的 70B、8 块 B200 一起跑 70B、同样 8 块、一批 64 人。拖上下文长度和批大小。Presets: 8B on the robot, 70B on one B200, 70B on 8 B200s and Same 8, batch of 64. Drag the Context length and Batch size sliders.
  • 下面的条是一个词元的时间花在哪：读参数、读键值缓存、计算、GPU 之间通信、零碎开销；旁边是每个用户每秒几个词元、整组 GPU 每秒一共几个词元。The bar below shows where one token’s time goes: reading the parameters, reading the KV cache, computing, communication between the GPUs and other overheads; beside it are the tokens per second for each user and the total tokens per second for the whole group of GPUs.

先玩：先看"一块 B200 上的 70B"：时间主要花在哪？换成 8 块一起跑：快了几倍，为什么不是 8 倍？把上下文拖到 128 000：哪一段变长了？最后选"一批 64 人"：每个人慢了多少，整组一共快了多少？Try first: Start with "70B on one B200": where does most of the time go? Switch to 8 GPUs running together: how many times faster is it, and why not 8 times? Drag the context to 128,000: which part gets longer? Finally choose "Same 8, batch of 64": how much slower is each person, and how much faster is the group as a whole?

这一步的要点：一个词元要把全部参数和键值缓存各读一遍，所以时间主要花在显存上；把模型切到几块 GPU 上能一起读，代价是每层都要通过 NVLink 交换两次结果。凑成一批，读一次参数能给很多人用。对机器人，网络往返常常比 GPU 里的几毫秒更要紧。The point of this step: Each token has to read all the parameters and the KV cache once, so most of its time goes on GPU memory; splitting the model across several GPUs lets them read in parallel, at the price of exchanging results over NVLink twice in every layer. With batching, one read of the parameters serves many people. For a robot, the network round trip often matters more than the few milliseconds inside the GPUs.

第 ⑨ 步 · 数据中心Step ⑨ · Data centres

为什么要那么多显存、那么多 GPU、那么多光纤Why so much memory, so many GPUs and so much fibre

机器人身上那块模块有 128 GB 内存、几十到一百多瓦。训练它用的模型、回答它那个难题的模型，却住在另一种地方：一栋楼里几万到几十万块 GPU，每一块都吃一千瓦左右的电。为什么要这么大？三件事叠在一起。The module on the robot has 128 GB of memory and draws from a few tens of watts to over a hundred. But the models it runs were trained somewhere quite different, and that is also where the model that answers its hard question lives: a building with tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of GPUs, each drawing about a kilowatt. Why does it need to be so big? Three things stack up.

第一，装得下。模型越来越大：开源的 Llama 3.1 最大的一个有 4050 亿个参数（Grattafiori 等 2024），光是用 FP8 存就要 405 GB，一块 GPU 的显存（一块 B200 约 180 GB）放不下。再加上每个用户的键值缓存（第 ⑦ 步），同时服务的人越多、对话越长，要的显存越多。训练时更夸张：除了参数本身（BF16，2 字节），每个参数还要存它的梯度（2 字节）、一份 FP32 的参数副本和优化器记的两份历史（共 12 字节），用混合精度训练时一共约 16 字节（Rajbhandari 等 2020）：一个 700 亿参数的模型，光这些就要 1.1 TB，还没算中间结果。First, fitting in memory. Models keep getting bigger: the largest open Llama 3.1 model has 405 billion parameters (Grattafiori et al. 2024), which need 405 GB just to store in FP8, more than one GPU’s memory can hold (a B200 has about 180 GB). On top of that comes each user’s KV cache (step ⑦): the more people served at once and the longer the conversations, the more memory it takes. Training is even more demanding: besides the parameter itself (BF16, 2 bytes), each parameter also needs its gradient (2 bytes), an FP32 copy of the parameter and the two histories the optimiser keeps (12 bytes together), about 16 bytes in all with mixed-precision training (Rajbhandari et al. 2020): for a 70-billion-parameter model these alone come to 1.1 TB, before counting any intermediate results.

第二，算得完。训练要的运算约是 6ND（第 ⑩ 步）。700 亿参数、15 万亿个词元：6 × 7 × 1010 × 1.5 × 1013 = 6.3 × 1024 次。一块 B200 用 BF16 的稠密峰值约 2.25 PFLOPS（NVIDIA），就算一直用上 40%，也要 7 × 109 秒，两百多年；一万六千块一起算，五天左右。Second, finishing in time. Training takes about 6ND operations (step ⑩). For 70 billion parameters and 15 trillion tokens: 6 × 7 × 1010 × 1.5 × 1013 = 6.3 × 1024 operations. One B200’s dense BF16 peak is about 2.25 PFLOPS (NVIDIA); even running at 40% of that the whole time, it would need 7 × 109 seconds, more than two hundred years. With 16,000 of them working together, it takes about five days.

第三，连得上。几万块 GPU 只有连在一起才是一台机器，可连接的办法各不相同，速度差得很远。分工的办法有四种，常常同时用：Third, staying connected. Tens of thousands of GPUs only become one machine when they are linked together, but the links come in different kinds, with very different speeds. There are four ways to divide up the work, often used together:

  • 数据并行：每块 GPU 一份完整的模型，各看不同的数据，每一步结束时把大家的梯度加起来平均。Data parallelism: each GPU holds a complete copy of the model and looks at different data; at the end of each step, all the gradients are added up and averaged.
  • 张量并行：把每一个大矩阵切开，几块 GPU 各算一块（第 ⑧ 步）。每一层都要交换结果，最依赖连线的速度和延迟。Tensor parallelism: each big matrix is cut up and several GPUs each compute one piece (step ⑧). Results have to be exchanged in every layer, so it depends most on the speed and latency of the links.
  • 流水线并行：把几十层分成几段，每段放在不同的 GPU 上，像流水线一样一批批往下传。Pipeline parallelism: the dozens of layers are divided into a few stages, each on different GPUs, and batch after batch is passed down from stage to stage, as on an assembly line.
  • 专家并行：混合专家模型的不同"专家"放在不同的 GPU 上，每个词元只被送到它要用的几个专家那里。Expert parallelism: the different "experts" of a mixture-of-experts model sit on different GPUs, and each token is sent only to the few experts it needs.
tar ≈ 2 (n − 1) / n · M / BWlink + 2 (n − 1) · τ

n 块 GPU 用环的方式把各自的 M 字节加在一起，每块大约要发出、收进两倍 M 的数据，所以时间约等于 2M 除以每块 GPU 的连线带宽，再加上 2(n − 1) 次"一跳"的延迟。When n GPUs add up their M bytes each around a ring, each GPU sends and receives about twice M of data, so the time is roughly 2M divided by each GPU’s link bandwidth, plus the latency of 2(n − 1) "hops".

环形全规约（Patarasuk & Yuan 2009）把数据切成 n 块，沿着环传两圈：第一圈每块 GPU 一边收一边加，传完时每块 GPU 手里都有一块已经加好的；第二圈把加好的块传给所有人。每块 GPU 收发的总量几乎不随 n 变，所以很省带宽；可跳的次数随 n 增加，GPU 一多，延迟这一项就显出来了。实际的库（NCCL）会按情况换成树形或分层的做法。Ring all-reduce (Patarasuk & Yuan 2009) cuts the data into n chunks and passes them twice round the ring: on the first lap each GPU adds as it receives, so that at the end each GPU holds one chunk that is fully summed; on the second lap the summed chunks are passed on to everyone. The total each GPU sends and receives barely changes with n, so it is very economical with bandwidth; but the number of hops grows with n, and once there are many GPUs the latency term starts to show. Real libraries (NCCL) switch to tree-shaped or hierarchical schemes depending on the situation.

tar
一次全规约的时间time for one all-reduce
n
参与的 GPU 数number of GPUs taking part
M
每块 GPU 要加起来的数据量，字节amount of data each GPU has to add up, in bytes
BWlink
每块 GPU 对外的连线在一个方向上的带宽，字节/秒bandwidth of each GPU’s external link in one direction, in bytes/s
τ
传一跳的延迟latency of one hop

数据并行训练 700 亿参数的模型，梯度用 BF16 是 M = 140 GB，每一步都要全规约一次（一块 GPU 装不下 70B 的全部训练状态，实际要像 ZeRO 那样把优化器状态和梯度分到各块 GPU 上存；每一步要交换的数据量差不多）。在一个 NVL72 机柜之内走 NVLink：NVIDIA 的 NVLink 带宽是按两个方向加起来标的（它给 Rubin 的写法是"3 TB/s 双向"，NVIDIA），所以 Blackwell 每块 GPU 的 1.8 TB/s 在一个方向上是 900 GB/s，n = 72 时 tar ≈ 2 × 71 / 72 × 140 GB / 900 GB/s ≈ 0.31 s。隔着机柜走每块 GPU 800 Gb/s（100 GB/s）的网卡（NVIDIA），约 2.8 s，慢 9 倍。所以实际训练会把梯度切碎、边算边传，把最费通信的张量并行关在 NVLink 连着的那一组里，跨柜子只做通信少的数据并行和流水线并行。In data-parallel training of a 70-billion-parameter model, the gradients in BF16 come to M = 140 GB, and every step needs one all-reduce (one GPU cannot hold the full training state of a 70B model, so in practice the optimiser state and gradients are spread across the GPUs, as ZeRO does; the amount exchanged per step is about the same). Inside one NVL72 rack this goes over NVLink. NVIDIA quotes NVLink bandwidth with both directions added together (for Rubin it writes "3 TB/s bidirectional", NVIDIA), so Blackwell’s 1.8 TB/s per GPU is 900 GB/s in one direction, and with n = 72, tar ≈ 2 × 71 / 72 × 140 GB / 900 GB/s ≈ 0.31 s. Across racks, through each GPU’s 800 Gb/s (100 GB/s) network card (NVIDIA), it takes about 2.8 s, 9 times as long. So real training cuts the gradients into pieces and sends them while it is still computing, keeps tensor parallelism, which needs the most communication, inside a group linked by NVLink, and across racks uses only data parallelism and pipeline parallelism, which need less communication.

带宽差这么多，是因为距离不同：芯片内、封装内、电路板上、一个机柜里、机柜之间，每往外走一层，线就更长，每传一个比特要的能量更大，能并排拉的线也更少。The bandwidths differ so much because the distances differ: within a chip, within a package, on a circuit board, within a rack, between racks. With each step outwards, the wires get longer, each bit takes more energy to send, and fewer wires can run side by side.

铜线和光纤Copper and fibre

一个机柜之内，GPU 之间靠铜线：NVIDIA 的 GB200 NVL72 把 72 块 GPU 用 NVLink 交换芯片连成"一块大 GPU"，合起来 130 TB/s（NVIDIA），铜缆只有一两米长。可在今天每条通道每秒两百多 G 比特的速度下，信号在铜线里走几米就衰减得认不出来了，机柜之间只能改用光：每根光纤两头各有一个光模块，把电信号变成激光、再变回来。一个十万块 GPU 的集群里，光模块数以十万计：按 OPN 对 NVIDIA 发布会的报道，一座 AI 工厂可能要 240 万个光模块、24 MW，平均每个约 10 W（OPN 2025）。现在的办法是把光的收发直接做进交换芯片的封装里，叫共封装光学（CPO），省掉中间那段长长的电线，NVIDIA 说功率效率能提高到 3.5 倍（第 ⑭ 步）。Within a rack, the GPUs are linked by copper: NVIDIA’s GB200 NVL72 uses NVLink switch chips to join 72 GPUs into "one big GPU", 130 TB/s in total (NVIDIA), over copper cables only a metre or two long. But at today’s speeds of more than 200 gigabits per second per lane, a signal in copper fades beyond recognition within a few metres, so between racks the links have to switch to light: each optical fibre has an optical transceiver at each end, turning electrical signals into laser light and back again. A cluster of 100,000 GPUs has hundreds of thousands of transceivers: according to OPN’s report on an NVIDIA launch event, one AI factory might need 2.4 million transceivers and 24 MW, about 10 W each on average (OPN 2025). Today’s answer is to build the optical sending and receiving straight into the switch chip’s package, called co-packaged optics (CPO), which cuts out the long stretch of electrical wiring in between; NVIDIA says this gives up to 3.5 times the power efficiency (step ⑭).

电和散热Power and cooling

一块 B200 最多 1000 W，一个 72 块 GPU 的机柜按 132 kW 设计供电和散热（Vertiv 2024），相当于上百户人家平时的用电；风扇吹不动这么多热，要用液体直接冷却芯片。全世界数据中心 2024 年用了约 415 太瓦时的电，约占全球的 1.5%，国际能源署估计到 2030 年会翻一倍多（IEA 2025）；今天最大的几个 AI 数据中心，单个已经在一吉瓦上下（Epoch AI 2026）。即便如此，电费在 AI 数据中心的总成本里只占一小部分：Epoch AI 估算，一个 1 GW 的 AI 数据中心每年约 85 亿美元的总成本里，电只占约 6 亿，服务器约 50 亿（Epoch AI 2026）。One B200 draws up to 1000 W, and a 72-GPU rack is designed for 132 kW of power and cooling (Vertiv 2024), about what more than a hundred households normally use; fans cannot carry away that much heat, so liquid cools the chips directly. Data centres worldwide used about 415 TWh of electricity in 2024, about 1.5% of the world’s total, and the International Energy Agency expects that to more than double by 2030 (IEA 2025); the largest AI data centres today are already around a gigawatt each (Epoch AI 2026). Even so, electricity is only a small part of an AI data centre’s total cost: Epoch AI estimates that of the roughly $8.5 billion a year that a 1 GW AI data centre costs in total, electricity accounts for only about $0.6 billion and the servers for about $5 billion (Epoch AI 2026).

  • 选一个模型大小、训练用的词元数、GPU 的型号和数量。上面是三笔账：装得下（参数、键值缓存、训练状态要几块 GPU 的显存）、算得完（训练要多少天）、连得上（一次全规约在一柜之内和跨柜各要多久）。Choose a model size, the number of training tokens, and the GPU type and number. The top part does three sums: Fits in memory (how many GPUs’ worth of memory the parameters, the KV cache and the training state need), Finishes in time (how many days training takes) and Stays connected (how long one all-reduce takes within a rack and across racks).
  • 下面画出这些 GPU 怎样一层层连起来：一块 GPU、一台八卡服务器、一个 72 卡的机柜、整个集群；哪里是铜线、哪里是光纤。旁边算出要多少个机柜、按每柜 132 kW 要多少电。拖每块 GPU 配几个光模块（这是假设，取决于网络怎么搭），看光模块一共要多少个、按平均每个 10 W 要多少电（10 W 是 OPN 那篇报道里两个数相除得到的平均；同一篇报道说光模块的电可能超过整个数据中心的一成，比这里算出的高，差在每个光模块的功率和每块 GPU 配几个）。Below, a drawing shows how these GPUs connect, level by level: one GPU, an 8-GPU server, a 72-GPU rack, the whole cluster; where the links are copper and where they are fibre. Beside it: how many racks are needed and, at 132 kW a rack, how much power. Drag the Optical transceivers per GPU slider (an assumption, which depends on how the network is built) to see how many transceivers there are in all and, at 10 W each on average, how much power they draw (the 10 W is the average from dividing two numbers in that OPN report; the same report says transceivers could take more than a tenth of a whole data centre’s power, more than is worked out here; the difference lies in the power per transceiver and how many each GPU has).

先玩：选 70B、15 万亿词元、1 万块 B200：要训练几天？一次全规约，跨柜比柜内慢几倍？把 GPU 加到 10 万块：要多少个机柜、多少电？光模块的电占了百分之几？Try first: Choose 70B, 15 trillion tokens and 10,000 B200s: how many days does training take? How many times slower is one all-reduce across racks than within a rack? Raise the number of GPUs to 100,000: how many racks, and how much power? What percentage of the power goes to the transceivers?

这一步的要点：数据中心要那么大，是因为模型和它的训练状态一块 GPU 装不下、一块 GPU 算不完，几万块 GPU 必须连成一台机器。越近的连线越快：机柜里用 NVLink 和铜线，机柜之间只能用光；电和散热成了新的瓶颈。The point of this step: Data centres are so big because one GPU can neither hold a model and its training state nor finish the computation in time, so tens of thousands of GPUs must be linked into one machine. The closer the link, the faster it is: inside a rack, NVLink and copper; between racks, only light will do. Power and cooling have become the new bottleneck.

第 ⑩ 步 · 越大越好？Step ⑩ · Is bigger better?

规模定律：好多少，代价是什么Scaling laws: how much better, and at what cost

为什么大家都在造更大的模型、更大的数据中心？因为过去几年反复验证了一件事：只要按比例同时加大模型、数据和算力，模型的预测误差就会沿着一条很平滑的曲线往下走，跨好几个数量级都不拐弯（Kaplan 等 2020）。这条规律叫规模定律。它让"多花十倍的钱，能好多少"可以事先估出来，于是有人敢一次投几亿美元去训练一个模型。Why is everyone building bigger models and bigger data centres? Because one thing has been confirmed again and again over the past few years: as long as you scale up the model, the data and the compute together in proportion, the model’s prediction error comes down along a very smooth curve that does not bend across several orders of magnitude (Kaplan et al. 2020). This regularity is called a scaling law. It lets you estimate in advance "how much better do we get for ten times the money", which is why people dare to put hundreds of millions of dollars into training a single model.

C ≈ 6 N DL(N, D) = E + A / Nα + B / Dβ

训练一个模型要的运算次数，约等于 6 乘参数个数、再乘训练用的词元数。训练完的损失，等于一个降不下去的底，加上一项随模型变大而变小的、一项随数据变多而变小的。The number of operations needed to train a model is about 6 times the number of parameters times the number of training tokens. The loss after training is a floor that cannot be lowered, plus one term that shrinks as the model grows and another that shrinks as the data grows.

第一行：训练时每个词元要算一遍前向（第 ⑦ 步：2N 次运算），再算一遍反向，求出每个参数该怎么改（大约是前向的两倍，4N），一共 6N；D 个词元就是 6ND。第二行的形式是 DeepMind 2022 年提出的（Hoffmann 等 2022，常叫 Chinchilla）：损失是模型预测下一个词元的"意外程度"，E 是语言本身的不确定性，再大的模型也消不掉；另外两项都是幂律，大一倍只少一点点，但稳定地少。算力 C 给定时，N 和 D 怎么分最划算，可以从这个式子里求出来：大致是每个参数配 20 个词元。论文原文给的常数，求出来约是每个参数 70 个词元，和它自己另外两种方法得出的 20 对不上；后来有人从论文的图里取出数据点重新拟合，得到的一组常数和 20 对得上（Besiroglu 等 2024），这里用的是这一组。常数换了数据就会变，所以用它比"大致多少"，不要比小数点后面。First line: in training, each token needs one forward pass (step ⑦: 2N operations) and then one backward pass to work out how each parameter should change (about twice the forward pass, 4N), 6N in all; for D tokens that makes 6ND. The form of the second line was proposed by DeepMind in 2022 (Hoffmann et al. 2022, often called Chinchilla): the loss is how "surprised" the model is when predicting the next token; E is the uncertainty in language itself, which no model, however large, can remove; the other two terms are power laws: double the model or the data and they shrink only a little, but steadily. For a given compute C, the best way to divide it between N and D can be worked out from this formula: roughly 20 tokens per parameter. The constants given in the original paper work out to about 70 tokens per parameter, which does not match the 20 from the paper’s own two other methods; later, others extracted the data points from the paper’s figures and refitted them, obtaining a set of constants that does match 20 (Besiroglu et al. 2024), and that is the set used here. The constants change when the data change, so use the formula to compare "roughly how much", not the digits after the decimal point.

C
训练用的总运算次数，FLOPtotal number of operations used in training, FLOP
N, D
参数个数；训练用的词元数number of parameters; number of training tokens
L
训练后在新数据上的损失（越小越好）loss on new data after training (lower is better)
E, A, B, α, β
拟合出的常数。这里用 Besiroglu 等重新拟合的 E = 1.82，A = 482，B = 2085，α = 0.348，β = 0.366；Hoffmann 等原文给的是 E = 1.69，A = 406.4，B = 410.7，α = 0.34，β = 0.28（论文附录 D.2）fitted constants. Here we use the refit by Besiroglu et al., E = 1.82, A = 482, B = 2085, α = 0.348, β = 0.366; the original by Hoffmann et al. gives E = 1.69, A = 406.4, B = 410.7, α = 0.34, β = 0.28 (Appendix D.2 of their paper)

先验证第一行：Llama 3 最大的模型有 4050 亿个参数，用 15.6 万亿个词元训练，6 × 4.05 × 1011 × 1.56 × 1013 ≈ 3.8 × 1025，正是论文自己报的训练运算量（Grattafiori 等 2024）。它的 8B 小模型用相近的配方、同样约 15 万亿个词元：C = 6 × 8 × 109 × 15 × 1012 = 7.2 × 1023。按每个参数 20 个词元，同样的算力最划算的是约 770 亿参数、1.5 万亿词元；Meta 也直说，小模型"训练得比算力最划算的要长得多"。用第二行粗算：8B、15 万亿词元，L ≈ 2.022；同样算力下最划算的那个（约 77B、1.5 万亿词元），L ≈ 1.968。损失只差 0.05，可后者每生成一个词元要贵近 10 倍。First, a check of the first line: the largest Llama 3 model has 405 billion parameters and was trained on 15.6 trillion tokens; 6 × 4.05 × 1011 × 1.56 × 1013 ≈ 3.8 × 1025, exactly the training compute the paper itself reports (Grattafiori et al. 2024). Its small 8B model used a similar recipe and likewise about 15 trillion tokens: C = 6 × 8 × 109 × 15 × 1012 = 7.2 × 1023. At 20 tokens per parameter, the best use of the same compute would be about 77 billion parameters and 1.5 trillion tokens; Meta says so outright: its smaller models are trained "for much longer than is compute-optimal". A rough estimate with the second line: for 8B and 15 trillion tokens, L ≈ 2.022; for the best model at the same compute (about 77B and 1.5 trillion tokens), L ≈ 1.968. The loss differs by only 0.05, but the latter costs nearly 10 times as much for every token it generates.

规模定律说的是训练时的账；用起来还有另一笔账：每生成一个词元要 2N 次运算、读一遍 N 个参数。模型大十倍，每个词元就贵十倍、慢十倍。所以今天的趋势是"把训练的力气花在一个用起来够快的模型上"，再用蒸馏（让小模型学大模型）、量化（用更少的位数）、混合专家（每个词元只用一部分参数）把用的成本压下来。Scaling laws are about the bill for training; using the model runs up a second bill: every token generated takes 2N operations and one read of all N parameters. Make the model ten times larger and every token becomes ten times as expensive and ten times as slow. So today’s trend is to "spend the training effort on a model that is fast enough to use", then bring the cost of use down with distillation (a small model learns from a large one), quantisation (using fewer bits) and mixture of experts (each token uses only part of the parameters).

还有一种"变大"发生在用的时候：让模型在回答之前先多想一会儿，写出一长串推理的词元，再给答案。多想的效果因题目的难度而不同：在小模型本来就有一定把握的题目上，把同样的算力花在多想上，能胜过一个大 14 倍的模型（Snell 等 2024）。代价是时间：多想一千个词元，在机器人的模块上就是几十秒。对机器人来说，这意味着一个取舍：规划"先拿杯子还是先开门"可以想几秒钟；手里的杯子开始打滑，只有几毫秒，根本来不及想。There is another kind of "scaling up" that happens at use time: letting the model think for a while before it answers, writing out a long chain of reasoning tokens and only then giving the answer. How much the extra thinking helps depends on how hard the problem is: on problems where a small model already has a fair chance, spending the same compute on thinking longer can beat a model 14 times larger (Snell et al. 2024). The price is time: a thousand extra tokens of thinking take tens of seconds on the robot’s module. For the robot this means a trade-off: planning "take the glass first, or open the door first?" can take a few seconds of thought; when the glass in its hand starts to slip, there are only a few milliseconds, far too little time to think.

机器人的规模定律还在找。大模型训练用的文字已经有十几万亿个词元（Llama 3 用了 15.6 万亿），机器人的动作数据却要一台台机器、一小时一小时地采，少得多；所以现在的机器人模型，大多先借用在图片和文字上训练好的大模型，再用相对少的机器人数据去教它动作（第 3 篇第 8 步）：π0 用了一万多小时的机器人数据（Black 等 2024），最大的公开数据集之一 Open X-Embodiment 汇集了 21 家机构的 22 种机器人（Open X-Embodiment 2023）。Scaling laws for robots are still being worked out. The text used to train large models already runs to more than ten trillion tokens (Llama 3 used 15.6 trillion), but robot action data has to be collected machine by machine, hour by hour, so there is far less of it. That is why most robot models today start from a large model already trained on images and text, then use a relatively small amount of robot data to teach it actions (page 3, step 8): π0 used more than 10,000 hours of robot data (Black et al. 2024), and Open X-Embodiment, one of the largest public datasets, brings together 22 kinds of robot from 21 institutions (Open X-Embodiment 2023).

先玩：算力从 1021 拖到 1025：损失降了多少？最划算的模型变大了几倍？再看下图：这个最划算的模型放到机器人上，每秒还能说几个词？Try first: Drag the compute from 1021 to 1025: how much does the loss fall? How many times bigger does the best model get? Then look at the lower chart: put this best model on the robot, and how many words a second can it still say?

这一步的要点：同时加大模型、数据和算力，损失沿幂律稳定下降，训练要的运算约是 6ND；可模型每大十倍，用起来每个词元也贵十倍、慢十倍。对数据中心，越大越好；对机器人，还要问"来得及吗"。The point of this step: Scale up the model, the data and the compute together and the loss falls steadily along a power law, with training taking about 6ND operations; but every time the model gets ten times bigger, each token also becomes ten times as expensive and ten times as slow to use. For a data centre, the bigger the better; for a robot, you also have to ask "will it be in time?"

第 ⑪ 步 · 机器人的一秒Step ⑪ · One second in the robot

每秒涌进来多少，每块芯片一个钟How much pours in each second, and a clock in every chip

回到厨房。机器人每一秒都在吞数据，量有多大，先按开场的配置算一笔账：Back to the kitchen. Every second, the robot is swallowing data. To see how much, let’s first do the sums for the set-up from the opening:

R = Σk Wk · Hk · ck · fknimg = (W' / p)²

每秒涌进来的原始字节数，等于每个传感器"每次的宽乘高乘每个点几字节、再乘每秒几次"，全部加起来。一张图变成模型的输入，先缩成边长 W' 的方图，再切成边长 p 的小块，每一块是一个词元。The raw bytes pouring in each second are the sum, over every sensor, of "the width times the height of each reading, times the bytes per point, times the readings per second". To become the model’s input, an image is first shrunk to a square of side W', then cut into small patches of side p; each patch is one token.

相机一帧就有几十万到近一百万个点，每个点三种颜色各 1 字节，每秒几十帧，所以相机压倒一切；IMU、关节这些每次只有几十个字节，次数再多也只是零头。模型不直接吃原始像素：图像先被缩小，再像切豆腐一样切成小方块，每块变成一个向量，和文字的词元排在一起（第 4 篇讲过视觉 Transformer）。A single camera frame has anywhere from a few hundred thousand to nearly a million points, each with three colours of 1 byte each, at tens of frames a second, so the cameras swamp everything else; the IMU, the joints and the like send only a few tens of bytes each time, so however often they do it, they are a rounding error. The model does not eat raw pixels directly: the image is first shrunk, then cut into small squares like a block of tofu, and each square becomes a vector that lines up alongside the text tokens (page 4 covered the vision Transformer).

R
原始数据率，字节/秒raw data rate, bytes/s
Wk, Hk, ck, fk
第 k 个传感器每次的宽、高（对相机是像素；对别的传感器取 1 × 1）、每个点几字节、每秒几次for sensor k: the width and height of each reading (in pixels for a camera; 1 × 1 for other sensors), the bytes per point, and the readings per second
nimg
一张图变成几个词元how many tokens one image becomes
W', p
