  • 每一行是一条路线，每一列是它冲着的一个问题：算的能耗、内存带宽、连线、延迟、功耗。有圆点的格子，表示它在这一列上有帮助。Each row is a route, and each column one of the problems the routes go after: energy per op, memory bandwidth, interconnect, latency, power. A dot in a cell means the route helps with that problem.
  • 每行右边一条，标出它走到了哪一步：实验室、原型芯片、早期产品、已经商用。A strip at the right of each row marks how far the route has got: lab, prototype, early product, in commercial use.
  • 点一行，下面写出它是什么、谁在做、长处、为什么还没落地，和来源、年份。Tap a row and below it you can read what it is, who is working on it, its strengths, why it has not landed yet, and the sources with their years.

先玩：哪几条路线同时冲着内存带宽？哪一条离大规模商用最近，为什么偏偏是它？对厨房机器人最有用的是哪一条，它卡在哪？Try first: Which routes all go after memory bandwidth? Which one is closest to large-scale commercial use, and why that one in particular? Which would be most useful to the kitchen robot, and what is holding it back?

这一步的要点：想换掉"把数搬来搬去"的路有好几条：在存储里算、把运算挪到存储旁边、用光来算、用光来传、学大脑只在有事时才算、用物理的随机性来抽样。它们分别冲着内存墙、搬数据的能耗、连线的电和机器人的电池；共同的难处是精度、容量、软件生态和量产，而且要在大模型上证明自己。离落地最近的是用光传数据和传感器里算。The point of this step: there are several routes for replacing "moving numbers back and forth": computing inside memory, moving the arithmetic next to memory, computing with light, carrying data with light, computing only when something happens, like the brain, and sampling with physical randomness. Between them they go after the memory wall, the energy of moving data, the power used by the links and the robot’s battery; the difficulties they share are precision, capacity, the software ecosystem and mass production, and they must prove themselves on large models. Closest to commercial use are carrying data with light and computing in the sensor.

第 ⑯ 步 · 地图Step ⑯ · Map

这些芯片、方法和模型，彼此是什么关系How these chips, methods and models relate to one another

前十五步讲到的，加上没来得及展开的，一共 96 个器件、芯片、方法和模型。它们跨了八十年：1947 年的晶体管、1958 年的集成电路、1960 年代的 CMOS 和摩尔定律，奠定了"把开关越做越小、越放越多"这条路；1980 和 1990 年代有了脉动阵列、FPGA 和"内存墙"这个词；2000 年代显卡变成了通用的并行计算机，CUDA 出现；2012 年以后深度学习、专用芯片和规模定律一起起飞；最近几年，从 HBM4、FP4、共封装光学，到视觉–语言–动作模型和实时分块，再到在存储里算、用光算，几乎每年都在添新东西。What the first fifteen steps covered, plus what there was no room to go into, comes to 96 devices, chips, methods and models. They span eighty years: the transistor of 1947, the integrated circuit of 1958, and CMOS and Moore’s law in the 1960s set the course of "making switches ever smaller and packing in ever more of them"; the 1980s and 1990s brought systolic arrays, FPGAs and the term "memory wall"; in the 2000s graphics cards became general-purpose parallel computers and CUDA appeared; from 2012 deep learning, accelerators and scaling laws took off together; and in the last few years, from HBM4, FP4 and co-packaged optics to vision-language-action models and real-time chunking, and on to computing in memory and computing with light, something new has been added almost every year.

  • 每个小块是一个器件、芯片、方法或模型，后面是年份。点它，下面展开说明：它是什么、长处和代价、代表文献，以及它和别的条目的关系；有关系的条目用虚线框出来。Each small block is a device, chip, method or model, followed by its year. Tap it and an explanation opens below: what it is, its strengths and costs, key references, and how it relates to other entries; related entries are outlined with dashed boxes.
  • 分组：在哪一层（器件、芯片、存储、连线、整机、软件、模型、机器人）、管什么（算、存、传、感知、时钟、控制、电、训练、推理）、是什么（规律、器件、架构、产品、标准、方法、模型）、本页的步、年代。一个条目跨好几层时，在每一组里都出现；点它，各处一起亮。Group by: Which layer (devices, chips, memory, links, systems, software, models, the robot); What it is for (computing, storing, moving data, sensing, clocks, control, power, training, inference); What kind (laws, devices, architectures, products, standards, methods, models); Steps of this page; Era. An entry that spans several layers appears in each of those groups; tap it and every copy lights up.

先玩：按"管什么"分组，看"传"那一组：它们分别在哪一层？再按"年代"分组：2020 年以后那一组为什么这么多？最后点"内存墙"，顺着虚线框走：有几条路线是冲着它去的？Try first: Group by "What it is for" and look at the "Moving data" group: which layer is each of them in? Then group by "Era": why does the group for 2020 onwards hold so many? Finally tap "The memory wall" and follow the dashed boxes: how many routes are aimed at it?

几条主线A few main threads

  • 开关越做越小，然后时钟停住了：晶体管（1947）→ 集成电路（1958、1959）→ CMOS（1963）→ 摩尔定律（1965、1975）→ 登纳德缩放（1974）。2005 年前后，电压降不下去了，时钟停在几 GHz，功耗成了上限（①）；后来的办法是把晶体管做成全环绕栅极、把供电挪到背面，一块芯片做不大就用芯粒拼（⑭）。Switches kept shrinking, then clock speeds stalled: the transistor (1947) → the integrated circuit (1958, 1959) → CMOS (1963) → Moore’s law (1965, 1975) → Dennard scaling (1974). Around 2005 the voltage could not be lowered any further, clocks got stuck at a few GHz and power became the limit (①); the later answers were gate-all-around transistors, moving power delivery to the back of the chip, and, when one chip cannot be made any bigger, building it from chiplets (⑭).
  • 搬数据成了主角：缓存 → 内存墙（1995）→ 屋顶线模型（2009）→ HBM。算力每两年涨到 3 倍、内存带宽只涨到 1.6 倍（③），所以 FlashAttention、分页的键值缓存、凑批这些软件办法，和 HBM4、在存储里算这些硬件办法，都在想同一件事：少搬一点（④、⑦、⑧、⑮）。Moving data took centre stage: caches → the memory wall (1995) → the roofline model (2009) → HBM. Every two years compute grows 3-fold and memory bandwidth only 1.6-fold (③), so software fixes such as FlashAttention, paged KV caches and batching, and hardware fixes such as HBM4 and computing in memory, are all after the same thing: moving a little less (④, ⑦, ⑧, ⑮).
  • 从通用到专用：阿姆达尔定律（1967）说并行有上限；脉动阵列（1982）说同一个数可以在一排运算单元里传着用；TPU（2015 年用上）和张量核心（2017）把它做进了芯片；今天的 Ironwood、Trainium、Cerebras、Groq 是在不同的地方取舍：多专用、存储放哪、能不能租得到（⑤、⑥、⑭）。From general-purpose to specialised: Amdahl’s law (1967) says parallelism has a limit; the systolic array (1982) says one number can be passed along a row of arithmetic units and used by each in turn; the TPU (in service in 2015) and tensor cores (2017) built this into chips; today’s Ironwood, Trainium, Cerebras and Groq make their trade-offs in different places: how specialised to be, where the memory goes, whether you can rent it (⑤, ⑥, ⑭).
  • 软件是护城河，也是突破口：用显卡做通用计算（2004）→ CUDA（2006、2007）→ AlexNet（2012）→ cuDNN 等库（2014）→ PyTorch。NVIDIA 的领先主要在这一层；Triton、XLA、ROCm 想让同一份代码跑在别家的芯片上（②、⑥）。Software is both the moat and the way in: general-purpose computing on graphics cards (2004) → CUDA (2006, 2007) → AlexNet (2012) → libraries such as cuDNN (2014) → PyTorch. NVIDIA’s lead lies mostly in this layer; Triton, XLA and ROCm aim to let the same code run on other companies’ chips (②, ⑥).
  • 把几万块芯片连成一台机器：NVLink → 环形全规约（2009）→ 张量并行、流水线并行、ZeRO → 72 块 GPU 的机柜 → InfiniBand 和以太网 → 共封装光学 → 光 I/O。离得越远，线越少、每个比特越贵，所以通信最多的并行要关在最近的那一圈里（⑧、⑨、⑭、⑮）。Joining tens of thousands of chips into one machine: NVLink → ring all-reduce (2009) → tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, ZeRO → the 72-GPU rack → InfiniBand and Ethernet → co-packaged optics → optical I/O. The farther apart, the fewer the wires and the dearer each bit, so the parallelism that talks the most has to be kept in the innermost circle (⑧, ⑨, ⑭, ⑮).
  • 机器人的那一半：晶振和 PTP 管时间、图像变成词元（⑪）；视觉–语言–动作模型、动作块、实时分块、快慢两个系统管"想"（⑫）；单片机上的电流环和 EtherCAT 管最快的那几级（⑬）；事件相机、神经形态芯片和传感器里算，是在源头少产生一点数据、只在有事时才算（⑮）。The robot’s half: crystal oscillators and PTP keep time, and images become tokens (⑪); vision-language-action models, action chunks, real-time chunking and fast and slow systems do the "thinking" (⑫); current loops on microcontrollers and EtherCAT handle the fastest levels (⑬); event cameras, neuromorphic chips and in-sensor computing produce a little less data at the source and compute only when something happens (⑮).

总结Summary

回到开头：厨房里的十秒钟，芯片里的一秒钟Back to the start: ten seconds in the kitchen, one second in silicon

不管是数据中心里的大模型，还是机器人身上的动作模型，算一次都是同一件事：把数从存储搬到运算单元，做乘法和加法，再把结果送出去。今天最贵的往往不是"算"，而是"搬"和"等"：模型要整个住在显存里，所以要大显存；逐词生成时每个词元都要把全部参数读一遍，所以要高带宽；一块 GPU 装不下、算不完，所以要几万块连在一起，连线越远越要用光；机器人身上只有一百瓦上下，却要在几十毫秒里看完、想完、动起来，所以把"想"拆成快慢两层，把最快的反应留给单片机。下表把每个词和这台机器人、这个例子里的数放在一起。Whether it is a large model in a data centre or an action model on a robot, every computation comes down to the same thing: move numbers from memory to the arithmetic units, multiply and add, then send the results on. Today the most expensive part is often not "computing" but "moving" and "waiting": the whole model has to live in GPU memory, so you need a lot of GPU memory; in decode, every token means reading all the parameters once, so you need high bandwidth; one GPU can neither hold it all nor get through the work, so tens of thousands are linked together, and the longer the links, the more they need light; the robot has only about a hundred watts on board, yet must see, think and start moving within a few tens of milliseconds, so the "thinking" is split into a fast and a slow layer, and the fastest reactions are left to microcontrollers. 开头的那些问题The questions we started with

  • 为什么要更大的显存、更大的内存？模型的每个参数都要住在 GPU 自己的显存里，隔着 PCIe 现搬要慢几十倍（②）；生成每个词元都要把它们全读一遍，所以容量决定"放不放得下"，带宽决定"一秒说几个词"（③）；对话越长、同时用的人越多，键值缓存越大，有时比模型本身还大（⑦）。训练时连同梯度和优化器状态，每个参数一共要约 16 字节（⑨）。Why do we need more GPU memory and more RAM? Every parameter of the model has to live in the GPU’s own memory; copying it across PCIe when it is needed is tens of times slower (②). Generating each token means reading all of them once, so capacity decides "will it fit" and bandwidth decides "how many words a second" (③). The longer the conversation and the more people using it at once, the bigger the KV cache, sometimes bigger than the model itself (⑦). In training, counting gradients and optimiser state, each parameter needs about 16 bytes in all (⑨).
  • 为什么数据中心要那么多 GPU 和光通信？一块 GPU 装不下、算不完：700 亿参数的模型用 15 万亿个词元训练，一块 B200 要两百多年（⑨）。几万块必须连成一台机器，而机柜之外铜线走不远，只能用光；光模块多到兆瓦级，于是把光做进交换机（⑭）。Why do data centres need so many GPUs and so much optical communication? One GPU can neither hold it all nor get through the work: training a 70-billion-parameter model on 15 trillion tokens would take a single B200 more than two hundred years (⑨). Tens of thousands must be joined into one machine, and beyond the rack copper cannot reach far, so only light will do; there are so many optical transceivers that they draw megawatts, so the optics are being built into the switches (⑭).
  • 大模型的一次计算，在硬件里怎么走一圈？请求经过网络和 CPU 排队，被凑成一批；每一层，每块 GPU 从 HBM 读自己那份权重和键值缓存，张量核心做乘加，再通过 NVLink 把部分结果加起来；最后一层打分、挑出一个词元，再回到第一层（⑧）。How does one computation of a large model make its way round the hardware? The request comes in over the network, queues on the CPU and is put into a batch; at each layer, every GPU reads its own share of the weights and the KV cache from HBM, the tensor cores do the MACs, and the partial results are added up over NVLink; the last layer scores the tokens and picks one, and then it is back to the first layer (⑧).
  • 为什么更大的模型、更多的数据更好，代价是什么？损失随两者按幂律稳定下降（⑩）；但模型每大十倍，用起来每个词元就贵十倍、慢十倍，所以今天常把小模型训练得远超"最划算"的量，再想办法省用的成本。Why are bigger models and more data better, and what does it cost? The loss falls steadily with both, following a power law (⑩); but every time the model gets ten times bigger, each token becomes ten times dearer and ten times slower to use, so today small models are often trained far beyond the "compute-optimal" amount, and then ways are found to cut the cost of using them.
  • 具身智能要什么硬件，未来要多快？看得多、来得及、记得住、带得动、不掉线（⑫）。一秒钟涌进 163 MB，几乎全是相机（⑪）；要在身上每秒十次地用一个 700 亿参数的模型边看边想，内存带宽至少要 1.75 TB/s、算力约 2.8 PFLOPS，是今天机器人模块的六倍多带宽，功率却得留在一百瓦上下。缺的主要是"每瓦的带宽"。What hardware does embodied AI need, and how fast will it have to be? It must see a lot, react in time, remember, run on a battery, and not freeze when the network drops (⑫). 163 MB pours in every second, almost all of it from the cameras (⑪); to look and think on board with a 70-billion-parameter model ten times a second, you need at least 1.75 TB/s of memory bandwidth and about 2.8 PFLOPS of compute: more than six times the bandwidth of today’s robot module, while the power has to stay around a hundred watts. What is mainly missing is "bandwidth per watt".
  • CPU、GPU、专用芯片、FPGA、单片机、IMU、存储，区别和联系是什么？都是晶体管做的，区别在把晶体管花在控制、运算还是存储上，以及每一拍做什么是否确定（⑤）；在机器人身上它们按快慢分工：越快、越要准时的环，越靠近电机、用越小越确定的芯片（⑬）。它们也共用同一条制造链，所以晶体管、封装、内存的前沿是大家共有的（⑭）。How do CPUs, GPUs, ASICs, FPGAs, microcontrollers, IMUs and memory differ, and how are they related? They are all made of transistors; the difference is whether the transistors are spent on control, arithmetic or storage, and whether what happens in each clock cycle is fixed (⑤). On the robot they divide the work by speed: the faster a loop and the more it must be on time, the closer it sits to the motor and the smaller and more deterministic its chip (⑬). They also share one manufacturing chain, so the frontier in transistors, packaging and memory belongs to all of them (⑭).
  • 为什么大多数人选 NVIDIA？CUDA 是什么？CUDA 是一种写法、一套编译工具和一大堆调好的库；NVIDIA 的领先靠近二十年的软件、连成整台机器的网络和产能。代价是通用芯片不是每件事都最省、耗电、贵，还容易被一家锁住；AMD 的 GPU，Google 和亚马逊的专用芯片，Cerebras、Groq、华为昇腾都已经是产品，难处多半在软件生态（⑥）。Why do most people choose NVIDIA? What is CUDA? CUDA is a programming model, a set of compiler tools and a large collection of tuned libraries; NVIDIA’s lead rests on nearly twenty years of software, the networking that joins GPUs into a whole machine, and production capacity. The costs: a general-purpose chip is not the most efficient at everything, it draws a lot of power, it is expensive, and it is easy to get locked in to one supplier. AMD’s GPUs, Google’s and Amazon’s accelerators, Cerebras, Groq and Huawei’s Ascend are all products already; their difficulties lie mostly in the software ecosystem (⑥).
  • 哪些还没商用的技术可能帮上忙？在存储里算、把运算挪到存储旁边、用光算、用光传、学大脑只在有事时才算、用物理的随机性来抽样；它们冲着内存墙、搬数据的能耗、连线的电和机器人的电池，难处在精度、容量、软件和量产，而且要在大模型上证明自己（⑮）。Which technologies not yet in commercial use might help? Computing inside memory, moving the arithmetic next to memory, computing with light, carrying data with light, computing only when something happens, like the brain, and sampling with physical randomness. They go after the memory wall, the energy of moving data, the power used by the links and the robot’s battery; the hard parts are precision, capacity, software and mass production, and they have to prove themselves on large models (⑮).

小测验Quiz

芯片里最长的一条路要 350 ps。时钟最快多少？调到 3 GHz 会怎样？The longest path in a chip takes 350 ps. What is the fastest the clock can run? What happens if you set it to 3 GHz?

fmax = 1 / 350 ps ≈ 2.86 GHz。3 GHz 的一拍只有 333 ps，比 350 ps 短，信号还没走完下一拍就来了，结果会算错（①）。fmax = 1 / 350 ps ≈ 2.86 GHz. At 3 GHz a clock cycle lasts only 333 ps, shorter than 350 ps: the next tick arrives before the signal has finished its path, and the results come out wrong (①).

频率从 2 GHz 提到 3 GHz，电压要从 0.8 V 提到 1.0 V。动态功耗变成几倍？To raise the clock from 2 GHz to 3 GHz, the voltage has to go up from 0.8 V to 1.0 V. By what factor does the dynamic power grow?

P ∝ V² f：(1.0 / 0.8)² × (3 / 2) = 1.5625 × 1.5 ≈ 2.34 倍，快了 1.5 倍，电却多花了一倍多（①）。P ∝ V² f: (1.0 / 0.8)² × (3 / 2) = 1.5625 × 1.5 ≈ 2.34 times. The chip is 1.5 times as fast, but the power more than doubles (①).

95% 的工作能加速 100 倍，剩下 5% 不能。整体快几倍？95% of the work can be sped up 100 times; the other 5% cannot. How many times faster is the whole job?

阿姆达尔定律：S = 1 / (0.05 + 0.95 / 100) ≈ 16.8 倍。剩下的那 5% 决定了上限：再快也超不过 20 倍（⑤）。Amdahl’s law: S = 1 / (0.05 + 0.95 / 100) ≈ 16.8 times. The remaining 5% sets the ceiling: however fast the rest gets, the whole job can never be more than 20 times faster (⑤).

CUDA 里 N = 10 000 个元素，每块 128 个线程。要多少个块？最后一块有几个线程闲着？In CUDA, N = 10,000 elements, with 128 threads per block. How many blocks are needed? How many threads in the last block sit idle?

⌈10 000 / 128⌉ = 79 块，一共 79 × 128 = 10 112 个线程，闲着 112 个；它们算出的 i ≥ N，核函数里那句判断让它们什么也不做（⑥）。⌈10,000 / 128⌉ = 79 blocks, 79 × 128 = 10,112 threads in all, so 112 are idle: the i they work out is ≥ N, and the check in the kernel makes them do nothing (⑥).

一个 70B 的模型用 FP8 存，放在机器人的模块上（128 GB，273 GB/s）。放得下吗？一个人用时每秒最多几个词元？A 70B model stored in FP8 is put on the robot’s module (128 GB, 273 GB/s). Does it fit? With one user, how many tokens a second can it produce at most?

70 GB 放得下；每个词元读一遍 70 GB，最多 273 / 70 ≈ 3.9 个词元每秒，说一句话要好几秒（③）。70 GB fits. Each token reads all 70 GB once, so at most 273 / 70 ≈ 3.9 tokens a second: one sentence takes several seconds (③).

一块 H100 用 FP8，稠密峰值 1979 TFLOPS，显存 3.35 TB/s。拐点在哪？一个人逐词生成时，能用上峰值的百分之几？An H100 running FP8 has a dense peak of 1979 TFLOPS and GPU memory at 3.35 TB/s. Where is the ridge point? When decoding for one user, what percentage of the peak can it use?

I* = 1979 / 3.35 ≈ 590 FLOP/字节。逐词生成 I = 2，只能跑出 2 × 3.35 = 6.7 TFLOPS，约 0.34%（⑦）。I* = 1979 / 3.35 ≈ 590 FLOP/byte. Decoding has I = 2, so it reaches only 2 × 3.35 = 6.7 TFLOPS, about 0.34% (⑦).

Llama 3.1 8B 的结构（32 层、8 组键值头、每头 128 维），键值缓存用 BF16，上下文 32 000 个词元时有多大？With the layout of Llama 3.1 8B (32 layers, 8 KV heads, 128 dimensions per head) and the KV cache in BF16, how big is the cache for a context of 32,000 tokens?

每个词元 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131 072 字节，乘 32 000 约 4.2 GB（⑦）。Each token takes 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131,072 bytes; times 32,000, that is about 4.2 GB (⑦).

8 块 GPU 张量并行跑一个 80 层的模型，每层两次全规约，每次 5 µs。一个词元光通信就要多久？8 GPUs run an 80-layer model with tensor parallelism, doing two all-reduces per layer at 5 µs each. How long does one token spend on communication alone?

2 × 80 × 5 µs = 0.8 ms，和每块 GPU 读自己那份参数的 1.1 ms 差不多：所以 8 块一起跑快不了 8 倍（⑧）。2 × 80 × 5 µs = 0.8 ms, close to the 1.1 ms each GPU takes to read its own share of the parameters: that is why 8 GPUs together are not 8 times as fast (⑧).

训练一个 8B 的模型，混合精度加 Adam：参数、梯度和优化器状态一共要多少显存？一块 B200 放得下吗？Training an 8B model with mixed precision and Adam: how much GPU memory do the parameters, gradients and optimiser states need in all? Will they fit on one B200?

16 × 8 × 109 = 128 GB；B200 约 180 GB，光这些放得下，可中间结果还要占地方，实际常要切到几块 GPU 上（⑨）。16 × 8 × 109 = 128 GB. A B200 has about 180 GB, so these alone fit, but the intermediate results need room too, and in practice the job is often split across several GPUs (⑨).

一个 10 亿参数的模型，按"每个参数 20 个词元"，最划算要多少词元、多少运算？For a model with 1 billion parameters, at "20 tokens per parameter", how many tokens and how many operations does the most cost-effective training take?

D = 2 × 1010 个词元，C = 6 × 109 × 2 × 1010 = 1.2 × 1020 次运算；和 Chinchilla 论文表里的 1B、202 亿词元、1.21 × 1020 一致（⑩）。D = 2 × 1010 tokens, C = 6 × 109 × 2 × 1010 = 1.2 × 1020 operations; this matches the table in the Chinchilla paper: 1B, 20.2 billion tokens, 1.21 × 1020 (⑩).

头部相机 1280 × 720、每个像素 3 字节、每秒 30 帧。每秒多少字节？一小时呢？The head camera: 1280 × 720, 3 bytes per pixel, 30 frames a second. How many bytes a second? And in an hour?

1280 × 720 × 3 × 30 ≈ 82.9 MB/s，一小时约 299 GB：一台相机就占了全部原始数据的一半多（⑪）。1280 × 720 × 3 × 30 ≈ 82.9 MB/s, about 299 GB in an hour: this one camera produces more than half of all the raw data (⑪).

两块芯片的晶振，一个快 10 ppm，一个慢 10 ppm。不对钟，多久会差出 1 ms？Two chips’ crystals: one runs 10 ppm fast, the other 10 ppm slow. Without clock synchronisation, how long until they are 1 ms apart?

两者相差 20 ppm，每秒差 20 µs，1 ms / 20 µs = 50 s：不到一分钟就差出一毫秒（⑪）。They differ by 20 ppm, so they drift 20 µs apart every second; 1 ms / 20 µs = 50 s: in under a minute they are a millisecond apart (⑪).

π0 一次出 50 个动作，机器人每秒执行 50 个，每执行完 25 个就重算一次。每秒算几次？每次最多能算多久？π0 outputs 50 actions at a time; the robot executes 50 a second and recomputes after every 25. How many times a second does it compute? How long can each computation take at most?

每秒 2 次；下一块必须在剩下的 25 个动作（0.5 s）执行完之前算好，π0 在台式机显卡上要 73 ms，来得及（⑫）。Twice a second. The next chunk must be ready before the remaining 25 actions (0.5 s) have been executed; π0 takes 73 ms on a desktop graphics card, so it makes it in time (⑫).

一块芯片标 2070 TFLOPS、最多 130 W；另一块标 12.4 TOPS/W。每次运算各花多少 pJ？能直接比吗？One chip is rated at 2070 TFLOPS and up to 130 W; another at 12.4 TOPS/W. How many pJ does each spend per operation? Can the two be compared directly?

130 / (2.07 × 1015) ≈ 0.063 pJ；1 / 12.4 ≈ 0.081 pJ。不能直接比：前者是 FP4、稀疏的峰值，后者是模拟芯片跑自己的语音模型时实测的芯片能效（8 位输入输出），不算片外的数字处理，精度、稀疏、算不算内存和换算电路都不一样（⑮）。130 / (2.07 × 1015) ≈ 0.063 pJ; 1 / 12.4 ≈ 0.081 pJ. They cannot be compared directly: the first is a sparse FP4 peak; the second is the chip’s energy efficiency measured while an analogue chip ran its own speech model (8-bit inputs and outputs), leaving out the digital processing off the chip. The precision, the sparsity, and whether memory and the conversion circuits are counted all differ (⑮).

想继续深入Further reading

  • Hennessy、Patterson，A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture：两位图灵奖得主讲摩尔定律和登纳德缩放怎么走到头、为什么要专用芯片（第 ①、⑤ 步）。Hennessy and Patterson, A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture: two Turing Award winners on how Moore’s law and Dennard scaling ran out, and why accelerators are needed (steps ① and ⑤).
  • MIT 6.004 Computation Structures：从晶体管、门电路到处理器和存储层次的公开课讲义（第 ①、②、③ 步）。MIT 6.004 Computation Structures: open course notes that go from transistors and logic gates to processors and the memory hierarchy (steps ①, ② and ③).
  • Sze 等，Efficient Processing of Deep Neural Networks：神经网络硬件的综述，数据怎么在芯片里流、为什么搬比算贵（第 ④、⑤ 步）。Sze et al., Efficient Processing of Deep Neural Networks: a survey of neural-network hardware: how data flows through a chip, and why moving it costs more than computing with it (steps ④ and ⑤).
  • NVIDIA，CUDA Programming Guide：CUDA 的官方教程，从核函数、线程块讲起（第 ⑥ 步）。NVIDIA, CUDA Programming Guide: the official CUDA tutorial, starting from kernels and thread blocks (step ⑥).
  • Gholami 等，AI and Memory Wall：算力和带宽各涨多快，为什么大模型卡在带宽上（第 ③、⑦ 步）。Gholami et al., AI and Memory Wall: how fast compute and bandwidth have each grown, and why large models are held back by bandwidth (steps ③ and ⑦).
  • Williams、Waterman、Patterson，Roofline：屋顶线模型的原始论文（第 ⑦ 步）。Williams, Waterman and Patterson, Roofline: the original paper on the roofline model (step ⑦).
  • Hoffmann 等，Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models：Chinchilla，规模定律里"模型和数据怎么分"（第 ⑩ 步）。Hoffmann et al., Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models: Chinchilla, the scaling-law answer to "how to divide the budget between model and data" (step ⑩).
  • Black 等，π0：一个视觉–语言–动作模型从图像到 50 Hz 动作的完整做法，附推理时间的分解（第 ⑫ 步）。Black et al., π0: the complete recipe for a vision-language-action model, from images to actions at 50 Hz, with a breakdown of its inference time (step ⑫).
  • 第 5 篇：环环相扣：机器人的六层和一级级的环、总线和时钟同步（第 ⑪、⑬ 步的背景）。Page 5: Loops Within Loops: the six layers of a robot, its loops nested level by level, buses and clock synchronisation (background for steps ⑪ and ⑬).
  • 上一篇：两秒钟的录音：采样、频谱和滤波，传感器数据是怎么变成数的。Previous page: Two Seconds of Sound: sampling, spectra and filtering; how sensor data turns into numbers.
本页约定：1 GB = 109 字节，1 TB = 1012 字节；不另外说明时，TFLOPS、PFLOPS 是不算稀疏的稠密峰值，NVLink 的带宽按 NVIDIA 的写法是两个方向加起来；芯片的规格以厂家 2026 年 11 月公开的数字为准，"发布"和"上市"分开说。厨房里的机器人是虚构的：它的传感器、计算模块和模型照着 2025 到 2026 年公开的产品和论文来配（见开场）。所有交互都在你的浏览器里实时计算，没有声音。Conventions on this page: 1 GB = 109 bytes, 1 TB = 1012 bytes; unless stated otherwise, TFLOPS and PFLOPS are dense peaks that do not count sparsity, and NVLink bandwidth is given NVIDIA’s way, with the two directions added together; chip specifications are the figures their makers had published by November 2026, and "announced" and "on sale" are kept apart. The robot in the kitchen is fictional: its sensors, compute module and models are chosen to match products and papers published in 2025 and 2026 (see the opening). Every widget is computed live in your browser; there is no sound.
